title_x: Entertaining Look at Top Designers at Work
text:
If you enjoy interior design, this show provides entertaining and educational insight into some of the design processes. For years I have enjoyed seeing the designs of Mary McDonald, Kathryn Ireland, Jeffrey Alan Marks, Nathan Turner, and Martyn Lawrence-Bullard in magazines and books that I have purchased of their work. Their rooms circulate frequently on pinterest and have popular appeal. They each have different approaches to design, and I admire them all. It is fun to see them in action. Oh, so that's who you are, I found myself thinking. The show features them in their homes, with clients, associates, and with family and or friends. It's a personal look. Obviously, the designers probably camp it up a little for the cameras. The show's purpose is to entertain as much, or more, as educate. And that's fine with me. I like some froth and fun while I'm learning.

I have helped friends and acquaintances with decorating some of their rooms. I always imagined it would be easier for a designer with more background and a reputation, but see from this show how difficult it is even for top designers. When it goes well, there's no more fun job as you co-create something magical to delight the client. It's like creating heaven on earth; when it doesn't go well, it's like hell on earth. I had to laugh at Jeffrey Alan Marks' comment that sometimes he thought his job was more difficult than being president.

What I particularly like about the show is that when you have four to five designers featured, and with the different projects they're working on, you have several installation days and reveals in one show. So, the pace is quick. I also love watching the designers shop for items. Once you've seen as much as they have, you know pretty instinctively what will work and look amazing. Yes, there is the occasional item you have to return, but you have a very clear sense of direction. It's fun to see their imagination and design sensibility at work. Their eyes are so well trained, they spot possibilities. This show illustrates not only how easy and natural it is for them to design something extraordinary, but the challenges and obstacles as well. Of course, some of the prices of items are a tad jaw-dropping. It's helpful to see high-end items, because your eye gets trained with quality images enabling you to replicate the style at a price that suits your budget. Great style doesn't have to be exorbitant. It is still fun to see high-end items.

I like to watch interesting and upbeat shows while on the treadmill, so was delighted to find this show via Amazon and could purchase the season for a reasonable fee. This is a real treat if you enjoy interior design and enjoy watching designers at work. Looking forward to Season 2 of this show. Hope they produce many more seasons as I will never tire of seeing these designers at work.
description: ['Millions of dollars and out-sized egos are constantly on the line as Bravo gives viewers an unprecedented look into the exclusive and affluent world of high-end interior designers in Million Dollar Decorators. This season will explore the work and personal lives of Los Angeles-based designers Martyn Lawrence Bullard, Kathryn Ireland, Jeffrey Alan Marks, Mary McDonald, and Nathan Turner.']

text:
If you like edgy, eccentric, original and complex mysteries, the quality continues in this second installment of the first season of the iconic Sherlock. Watson seems more relaxed and at home in Sherlock's company and you can see their relationship meld right before your eyes. There's a mysterious murder of a banker with graffiti spray painted on the wall--why was the banker murdered and what does the graffiti mean offers a tantalizing puzzle for Sherlock.

In these episodes a series of crimes are attempted, and Sherlock has to discern a pattern of connection in order to solve them. His life and Watson's are usually put at risk, his apartment is invaded or damaged, and there's often an on-foot chase scene. Oh--and he is usually rude to a number of folks but manages to put them in their place with his superior intellect and wit.

It's a thoroughly enjoyable ride and the chemistry between Sherlock and Watson is palpable--hope there's many more seasons of this delightful mystery.
description: ["Sherlock Holmes, an analytical deduction fanatic, is helping the police out with their enquiries for fun, when he runs into potential flatmate Dr John Watson, fresh from serving in the war in Afghanistan and sporting a limp. In spite of Watson's initial scepticism, Holmes' brilliant mind and dangerous lifestyle offer the stimulation he craves, and the two quickly forge an alliance. Sherlock provides the inspired leaps of intellect, while Watson keeps his friend's flights of fancy grounded - it's the perfect partnership. Uplifting, action-packed and highly entertaining, with sparky scripts and unforgettable performances by the two leads, this is Sherlock for a new generation."]

title_x: A work of fiction- but still a good story
text:
In real life Kuklinski beat his wife all the time and his children and wife hated him, but I enjoyed this film and it has some good performances. I would've given it 4 stars if it wasn't for the note that comes up after the film is done which I will explain later.

The film makes you feel some empathy for the Iceman who is portrayed as a saint when it comes to his family- but the truth is very different. In reality, he often beat his wife so badly that she suffered miscarriages and broken bones. His wife tried breaking up with him when they were just dating, but he cut her in the back of the neck with a hunting knife and threatened to kill her if she dared leave him... and that's why she ended up marrying him. Not out of love, but out of fear. His daughters hated him so much that at least one of them plotted to poison him by putting something in his food. The only people who wanted this man dead more than the mafia bosses was his own family. In an interview his former wife said: "I will regret for the rest of my life, that I didn't just tell him the bastard he is and how much I hate him. I wish the last words he'd heard had been how much I hated his guts." Some loving family man, huh? But none of this really bothers me because these based on true story films are often full of misrepresentations and making the lead character someone to empathize with makes the experience more engaging for the viewer. As long as you keep these expectations you can enjoy these types of films as simply good movies without holding them up to any standard of truth.

But here is the thing that I do think is a big deal: After the movie ends the director flashes a note on screen stating that Kuklinski never saw his family again. This is a flat out lie. Kuklinski's wife continued to visit him in jail for almost a decade after his incarceration. According to her out of fear for her children since she thought that despite him being imprisoned he could still have someone on the outside cause harm to her. And she secretly recorded (with the help of a film production office) many of the phone conversations between he and she after he had gone to prison where the recordings show that he did he theaten her over the phone. When he was dying his wife took one of their daughters to visit him in the prison hospital also. I can excuse the director attempting to make the audience feel sorry for the lead CHARACTER, but I cannot excuse the director's blatant attempt to make the audience feel sorry for the REAL man, by printing the lie that he never saw his family again at the end of the film. Creating false scenes in a movie to make a good story are one thing, but the statements written at the end of a film are definitely meant to make the viewer believe something that occurred in reality. The statement that flashes across the screen stating that he never saw his family again was a flat out deception meant to evoke sympathy and I do not support it. If you ever meet director Ariel Vromen, don't take him at his word for anything.

For a final note I have cut and pasted the following from an article on the final hours of the iceman.

"as Richard Kuklinski's life finally slipped away, he became conscious long enough to ask doctors to make sure they revived him if he flatlined. But before she left, Barbara had signed a "do not resuscitate" order. A week before his death, in the early hours of March 5 2006, the hospital called Barbara to ask if she wished to rescind the instruction. She did not."

title_x: Even if you're not into this genre you'll still find reasons to like "Thor"
text:
I usually don't really like superhero movies as they are often rife with bad acting, unworthy scripts, and 2 dimensional characters; Special effects are often used as a way to hide the fact that there is not much of a story. Having said that- Thor fairs fairly well as far as this genre goes. Primarily due to the character Loki and the brilliant actor who portrays him.

Whether you are someone who lived under the shadow of a sibling or someone who felt lied to & betrayed by family.. whether you're someone who felt they weren't ever given a fair chance growing up or someone who was raised by a cold and restrictive parent.. or whether you were just someone who has felt like an outsider for much of their lives, chances are you're going to feel some sort of affinity toward Loki. And lets face it. This is going to mean a huge part of the population. Is there any wonder people gravitate toward this character unlike any other? Out of all the superhumans in the marvel universe thus far, Loki is by far the most human.

Thor is an oaf who's idea of fun is literally pounding his way through things. At the beginning especially, he is completely ruled by his ego and emotions. This changes somewhat through the course of the movie. Though not necessarily stupid, Thor is not really intelligent either. His idea of war includes no forethought and no strategy. What Thor does have aside from his massive structure is a lot of heart and conviction so he's overall a decent human being with a strong sense of self. Conversely Loki is a guy who thinks before he acts. Though he has a mischevious side, he is very intelligent (and at least at first) is able to put aside his ego and emotions for the greater good- that is until he finds out his entire life is a lie and he basically snaps. At the risk of sounding like someone who is excusing Loki's very serious misdeeds- one might even go as far as to say that Loki's "turn" is merely an exercise in reaching out for another identity after he so abruptly lost his.

The movie is not perfect by far. In fact, if it weren't for Loki it would've been a bit of a throw-a-way like most other movies of this genre. Chris Hemsworth makes a great Thor, but the script fails him sometimes. The romance between Thor and Jane is difficult to swallow. The idea that a brilliant physicist falls head over heels for a witless oaf like Thor (as he can be described in the beginning of the movie) just because he fills out his shirt well is a hard sell and unfortunately, this film doesn't even bother to try to sell it. Thor's interest in Jane is also a bit of a mystery as they have nothing in common. We're simply asked to accept this romance without ever being given any reason to care whether or not they come together - or stay together for that matter. Some scenes were choppy. Though not a perfect movie, it is by far the best superhero movie I've personally seen to date.

title_x: Classic Stalin Era  AgitProp Reflecting a Greater Truth
text:
While there should be no denying as to the suffering of the Soviet peoples under Nazi occupation (Nazi ideology called for their enslavement and ultimate eradication, thus prisoners of war from the USSR were routinely starved and worked to death), neither should we ignore the role of Stalin in the near defeat of the USSR - he trusted Hitler to keep his word in their mutual non-aggression treaty, hoping for several years peace in which to rebuild the Army he had devastated with his paranoid purges. All that aside, this film capitalises on the work of Red Army photographers and cinematographers. Like films produced by Allied servicemen in the West and the Pacific, it brings a gritty realism to a titanic struggle between great warring powers.

Orel, or Kursk as it is known in the West was one of the great turning points of the war against Nazism and the last time the USSR would fight a defensive battle. The Kursk salient was an all too enticing trap laid for Germany by the Soviet general staff. Knowing Germany's penchant for "Kesselschlacht" or cauldron battles, efforts to rapidly surround and immobilize large elements of the enemy and then pound them into surrendering, the Soviet's looked at their maps and saw a bulge in the lines that the German's could not overlook.

Kursk was a great bulge in the lines were German forces faced against Russian's on 3 sides. The Soviet forces within the bulge, or salient, appeared ripe to be cut off and the spaces turned into a cauldron, as the German's referred to it. Instead the Red Army in just a few weeks as Winter was melting into Spring, created an immense, densely layered defense utilising both well established infantry positions with enormous numbers of both anti-tanks guns and artillery, all designed to trap the Germans in a cooking pan of a Soviet design. Add to this Soviet armour in the form of the famed T-34 and KV tanks - more than a match for the vast majority of tanks fielded by Germany, and over-matched slightly by the new Panther and the rare Tigers - both of which suffered from the German penchant for over-design and elaborate engineering solutions to simple problems. This was so bad an issue with these new models that they required much higher levels of maintenance, leaving many of both models behind the lines in repair yards. Hitler himself delayed the battle, giving the Soviets desperately needed time to improve their trap, in order to bring new Tiger tanks to the battle. Indeed some fought in the battle, but most broke down before the battle even began.

While Soviet tactics were sound, the multi-layered defenses they established were extremely costly in terms of Soviet wounded and killed. While foot soldiers were not sent forward with one rifle for two or three men as they were at Stalingrad and a number of other Soviet battlefields, planners needed the first layers of defense to fail, leading the Germans further into the defenses, thus to be cut off and encircled. They were not afraid to sacrifice thousands for the goal of a German defeat. In the end the plan to encircle the Germans actually failed, with German forces breaking free, but it was nonetheless a costly defeat for the Germans. In open battle, utilising all the tactical prowess with artillery and armour for which German armies were known and feared, they were nonetheless defeated and forced from the field into retreat.

The film shows only little of all this, a moving armoured battle taking place over many miles of terrain is a hard thing for cameras to capture. Instead, perhaps rightly, the film sticks to a broader story, focusing on the heroic nature of this defense of the motherland. Indeed, Stalin himself had turned from the early propaganda of the war and its reliance on a Red vocabulary about a "people's revolutionary army" defending a "worker's paradise." Instead he and his propagandists turned to an older, more nationalistic terminology that spoke of the родина and отчизна - homeland and motherland and emphasized the defense of family and land.

Stalin's foolish standing order of no surrender, no retreat - as frustrating to his generals as the same order was when later given by Hitler to the German officer corps, may have been tactically disastrous at times, but from an ideological point of view it was brilliant. Stalin tied this order to a charge of treason and a clear position that to retreat was to endanger the motherland. i9deological training officers made it clear that every soldier was fighting, not for an ideological abstraction like "workers," or "the Party," but for his wife, his sweetheart, his mother, for the land where he or she was born and on which they all stood. As a resurgent Red Army passed through the villages and cities where they had once been defeated (as shown in this film), places remade by the Germans into immense charnel houses, they were seeing what well could have been their own homes. Indeed the murderous nature of the German occupation of lands they sought to eventually repopulate with German colonists -- as the Nazis had planned for virtually all of Europe from the German border east to the Ural mountains--would eventually redound to Germany as a crushing, vicious Soviet occupation of the Nazi Reich. I can think of no other modern army where officers willingly accepted hearing their troops scream a battle cry of VENGEANCE, shouted as they fought.

The film here is not polished, but then it wasn't meant for YT or network air time. The images were shot on miserable cameras on poor film stock, but they are images that spoke to the heart of an angry, suffering people. Not just soldiers, but workers, men, women and children putting in 16 hour days in defense plants, coal and iron mines, and all the other logistical centres of a nation at war for its very life. That audience is easy to forget today, just as we in America forget that in spite of our losses at D-Day and at the Rhine, and in spite of America supplying the USSR with tens of thousands of truck and aircraft, it was the USSR that defeated Nazi Germany. They were not alone, but it was their vengeful armies that led the way to Berlin against far greater forces than ever faced by the US or Britain. To put it in bloody terms, more than 8 of every 10 German soldiers and airmen killed in the war died on the Eastern front at the hands of the Red Army.

title_x: Too Busy Resuscitating Myth To Allow Francis Scott Key On the Screen
text:
Please don’t accept this pious retelling of American mythology as an accurate history of either Francis Scott Key or the War of 1812. It is neither. The producers of this video were too busy ducking and weaving away from the reality of his life, politics and accomplishments to let very much real history show.

Concerning the war, "Proof through the Night" mumbles quickly past the complex issues that stood between the American Republic and the British Crown. Indeed, no mention is made that America entered into its first war of choice when its opponent was bogged down fighting Napoleon. Planners in Washington had hoped that the United States could annex Canada while Britain was to overwhelmed by its war with France to reply. As is often the case in war planning, leaders often entertain fond hopes as if they were facts. Britain responded to American aggression with sufficient land and naval forces to threaten the very existence of our Republic. The burning of Washington, and the attack on Baltimore was British retribution for the USA's sacking and burning of York, then capital of Upper Canada. This video makes only passing notice of the fact that Francis Scott Key was a vigorous opponent of the war, rejecting both its timing and America's chances for success.

Concerning Key himself, while supposing itself a biography, this video much more resembles a hagiography. Francis Scott Key was a complex man, a poet of moderate ability, and an accomplished attorney. Though never a functionary, he served several presidents both as an emissary (as occasioned his brief detention aboard a British warship during the battle at Fort McHenry) and legal advocate, which led to his involvement in the prosecutions following the Aaron Burr affair. It might also be mentioned that Key’s brother-in-law Joseph Nicholson,was an officer serving as commander of one the militia's at Fort McHenry during the battle, and that is with this man who first had the poem printed for distribution to the public under the title of “Defence of Fort McHenry.”

Of his personal life a great deal is known. His involvement with issues of slavery led to his opposition to abolitionism, and not just, as it suggested in this video, because of that movement's occasional turn towards violence. Key was a slaveowner, and while it is true he freed a number of his slaves over the course of his life, he also purchased slaves. He also defended the practice of slavery in court. Like many in the South, he believed some of the practices associated with slavery were evil and would cause the eventual end of that societal madness. But, he did not believe in nor foresee American society as ever being other than White. He was a leading advocate for the return of freed slaves to Africa, and was a founding member of the American Colonization Society, rejecting any notion of what we would today call integration or multi-racialism. Shortly after his death, the Society achieved one of its greatest goals, that being the establishment of Liberia as a new colony in Africa for the resettlement of freed slaves. It was this movement that put him at odds with abolitionism, not violence, as is claimed by the video. The film mentions his defence of Native American treaty rights in Alabama as a negotiator for Pres. Andrew Jackson. Jackson's defence of those rights was maintained purely on constitutional grounds. Jackson was concerned with maintaining the authority of the national government, not preserving land for Native Americans. Indeed, Jackson was to sign the "Indian Removal Act" which would lead to the forcible exile of Native Americans from the Southeast to the so-called "Indian Territory," west of the Mississippi. A a friend and advisor to Pres. Andrew Jackson, it can be seen that both these men, like many others of their age, viewed the possibility of relations with non-whites to be impossible for America, whether they be former slaves or Native Americans.

As a film biography this video is the worst kind of revisionist history. It rarely lies outright. Rather it omits and misdirects. It attempts to elide the specters of racism and slavery that are central aspects of Francis Scott Key's legal and political ambitions. Born too late to have served in the American Revolution, Francis Scott Key was part and parcel of a triumphalist second-generation of political leadership in this country, a leadership that failed to harness the nation's energies to deal justly or equitably with issues of race, that ran roughshod over Native American nations, Canada () and Mexico, where the US first supported and then annexed the Republic of Texas, leading to the Mexican American war which redrew the map of North America in favour of the US. As an advisor and friend of American presidents, a capable, politically astute lawyer in Washington, Francis Scott Key was more than a "reluctant patriot," as he was called by author Norman Gelb, he was also among America's first and foremost political operators.

title_x: A personal, open letter to the Wachowskis
text:
Wow. Lana and Andy, I loved this movie. This movie is 10 years ahead of its time. Literally.

So...you really should have waited 10 years to release this movie. I'm glad you did it in 2015, because it meant a lot to me, but because of all of the negative ratings, it's really going to cramp your style for your next movie release. And, I'm sorry, You both are no Michael Bay. You're the real thing, and so you really can't release stuff that gets 3 stars with the critics and have an easy time getting 200M for a budget for your next movie. And, above everything else, I want you to release a new movie every 12-24 months. I don't care if it has the budget of Bound. Please, please keep making movies.

The biggest reason that I loved this movie is the reason why I loved Sci-Fi in the 70's and 80's. It's because this movie blew away my paradigms of the world, and expanded my thinking into what is possible and what the future holds. I actually haven't had an experience like this with a movie since the Matrix Reloaded. I had given up on science fiction and movies in general. My cynicism over the last decade can be attributed almost solely to Star Wars Episode I. But, with this movie, you've restored my faith in movies. Because of you, and this movie, I'm going to start watching a lot more movies than I have over the last 10 years. So, I cannot thank you enough for making this movie.

But...you made the movie just a stitch too fast-paced for 2015. The pacing of this film will be much better for 2020 audiences (or 2025). Plus, there aren't enough new-agey folks out there yet to accept your past-lives message. As far as I can tell, those are the only two valid criticisms of your awesome, excellent film. If there were a way to pre-order front row tickets to your next movie, I would do it now, and rent the whole theater.

text:
You've seen this, haven't you?

The CGI and related animation was often amazing, occasionally disappointing. The bridge (Thor readers know what I mean) connecting Asgard and Earth, was like a bad disco floor against a backdrop that was busy with flashing lights. That's not only a technical problem, but also, poor design. While a rainbow bridge might have felt a little too "Smurfy," work is still needed.

Plot
The gist is Thor is about to be crowned king in a lavish ceremony. His rock star attitude is tolerate because he is basically a decent guy. It is disrupted by the Frost Giants. Loki convinces Thor to wage war against the wishes of Odin, and they, with a few others, go to kick some icicle tail.

It gets seriously out of hand, and Odin banishes Thor to Earth. His hammer, the Mjolnir, is sent too, but only a man of Arthurian purity can pick it up. Thor's no longer fit to do it, nor can any of the humans who try. The sword, so to speak, stays in the stone.

Meanwhile, Loki is provocating war in Asgard with the Frost Giants, claiming Odin is dead (he's not), and ascending to the throne.

What happens next is why the movies matters.

Overall, it works. In short, like Iron Man, Thor is a story of a powerful person let their arrogance cause havoc. He realizes it, is humbled, and uses his powers for good. Simple as that, and, on this level, it works.

Weaknesses are in how they push the plot. For example: The romantic subplot is incomplete. Thor falls for Jane too deeply, too quickly. She's too easily accepting that he's a god.

Loki's intentions go from sneaky, to evil, to confusing. I left the theater with no idea what he was trying to accomplish.

It, more or less, follows the key Marvel comic book line. I won't go through the differences as the most not only needs to stand on its own, but comic are so often retconned (Retroactive continuity) to work in another era or media, it isn't worth deliberating.

Casting
Chris Hemsworth as Thor - Completely Thor. Superhero films has suffered from brilliant and horrible casting (Brandon Routh as an effeminate, unmasculine Clark Kent/Superman was the worst). Not here. Hemsworth fit the suit, the attitude. He's sexy without being raunchy, arrogant yet likable, humble but not a wimp.

Anthony Hopkins as Odin - Wow. Think of this as compared to Marlon Brando as Superman's dad, Jor-El. Who would have thought they would do a comic book movie? Hopkins is completely believable as Odin. A few lines should have been rewritten (watch near the end for a "should haven't been deleted Hallmark Afterschool Special" scene), but he masters even the thinnest lines.

Natalie Portman as Jane Foster - She works as the generic attractive brunette. You might not mind that she's there, but a half dozen other actresses could have stepped in.

Tom Hiddleston as Loki - He fits it. Not so evil, but by no means good. His role is something that of the serpent in Eden. He is a tempter, liar and thief.

Stellan Skarsgård as Dr. Erik Selvig - Like Portman, he did a fine, yet unremarkable job as Foster's mentor.

To compare it to other superhero movies around that time: Iron Man and the Batman movies are more sophisticated, but also darker and for older audiences. It misses the banter and emo-romance of Spiderman, and retro-cheesy fun of Superman. That's not a bad thing.

Anthony Trendl

Julie Andrews voices the dragon, Karathen. Karathen is not really a dragon, but she serves that role. Why Andrews was picked, I don't know. That's not a criticism of her so much as it is of casting.

There are other big names in this: Dolph Lungren and Willem Dafoe, for example, but the writing and directing make this nothing more than a forgettable Saturday matinee action flick.

The production values are weak and cliche. Atlantis looks like a toy model shot in close-up with characters green screened in. Imagine the old Godzilla series shot with better film.

title_x: Movie is as Good as the Book
text:
There's no movie without the book, and the book, to say the least, is an American classic. Harper Lee's book is handled tastefully and consistently. In other words, the movie is as good as the book.

"To Kill A Mockingbird" is more than the usually discussed issues of racial bigotry and the human condition under trial. Don't let me take away from those values at all, but Harper Lee has written a book transcending a literary social commentary. She has written a love story.

A love story? huh? Who gets married? Does anyone kiss? Are there passages of deep romance? No, no, no. None of that. Try instead family love.

Atticus is the kind of single dad we need to see more of in this generation. He cares for his children so much that he protects them from the fires of his grown-up life of representing an innocent man. He protects them from the full impact of his neighbor's lies. He shows them how to love them, even though he knows his neighbors hate him and the love of fellow man he represents.

If all Atticus, the father, did, was love the innocent man, he would be doing a good thing, but he demonstrates love and allows dignity (when possible) for the ones persecuting the innocent. He shows he is a big man, and his children mimic this sense of understanding.

Deeply rooted in the memories of his children, the story has a gentle subtext of growing up. You can almost taste the lemonade of the porch and smell the flowers in nearby gardens. This, in the movie, though, comes across as more Norman Rockwell than is accurate.

Gregory Peck, as Atticus, claims he played himself, making the role easier, perhaps, for him. Either way, he seemed perfectly cast.

Scout comes across perhaps more wise and courageous than the average six year-old, but it works in the context of the movie.

Arthur "Boo" Radley, played masterfully by Robert Duvall, is often forgotten as Gregory Peck's role overshadows his, but is one of the real heroes.

Tom Robinson, as played by Brock Peters who later had roles in Star Trek films, had the challenge of being a beaten down black man in an era and culture of rampant racism. The challenge was to do so without being a caricature. He pulls this odd.

Lee's power as an author here is that she does let her statements about humanity overtake the story. Rather, she lets the story tell the story, and she just writes down what happened in her imagination.

Her characters are not paste-up Southern children or adults, but complex characters all of us relate to (even me up here near Chicago!). Relationships are embedded in the depth of being neighbors. This creating a milieu of angst in Atticus' children when they see the adults warring in court and out of court in matters of truth.

I fully recommend "To Kill A Mockingbird," and think to give it the best reading possible, examine how interwoven the story is with its various cultures and characters. The power of Lee's message will be plenty clear.

Anthony Trendl

title_x: The Best Modern Western Produced In Many years
text:
This is one of the best modern westerns that I've seen in a long time. Mads Mikkelsen does his best "Squint" Eastwood imitation by muttering few words and letting his expressions and actions tell his story. The lovely Eva Green isn't so lovely playing her character since her backstory involves being kidnapped and mutilated by Indians prior to marrying into the wrong outlaw mob. You may recognize/remember Eva from her parts as a Bond Girl and appearing as the main character in "Penny Dreadful". Having her tongue cut out by the Indians resulted in her communication being limited to facial expressions, something that this accomplished actress does quite well.

The plot is well thought out and presented, the western scenery is beautiful but harsh, and the brutality towards the towns-people is a bit over-the-top -- but there are reasons for this. It appears that the main bad guy (played by Jeffery Dean Morgan) was recently an accomplished Indian fighter, is now in a unique position of power, and he treats everyone in his fiefdom with the same violent passion. Only one person among the towns-people has the courage and ability to sort out right from wrong, but his actions take him deeper into a trap where there appears to be no way out. Fortunately his brother gives him the opportunity to get the upper hand and seek retribution, to destroy the brutal reign of the outlaws, and to free the non-speaking but still beautiful Eva Green.

Rather than ruin your viewing experience by telling you how everything comes together, and give you spoilers that will help you understand the reasons for all this violence, let me just say that everything makes sense at the end. This is not a pretty story. However this movie tells the tale of greed and violence that is still relevant to this day. Superbly under-acted by a great cast.

text: My father’s best friend died after surviving The Battan Death March. A survivor of the camp reported his death so the Army returned the remains of James Azey Hughes to his family in Graniteville, South Carolina. I have read books and watched many documentaries on the Pacific War. This series contains actual film and photos never before seen.  This is by far the best presentation of key events and US strategy for winning the war.  They present a lot of the story thru the old films.  A good touch is the inclusion of pre-war films which are included.  After watching all the killing and wounding involved in taking just a few islands, it reinforced the justification for the decision to use the atomic bomb. It should be noted here that a subtitle to this movie might be called "The Case of the Vanishing Accent" as in a few scenes Strathairn has the Irish accent of his character yet in most he does not. Suffice it to say, that's a little picky but certainly noticable.

Both my wife and I enjoy the movie. Not only was it entertaining but well played out and written. There's a bit of underlying information that most people know little about. The times were the times and the people were the people. Interesting and Enjoyable to watch, is my verdict.
description: ['When a series of package bombs target prominent politicians and businessmen, Agent William Flynn (Academy Award-nominee David Strathairn) becomes immersed in an investigation that uncovers an anarchist plot to destroy democracy. Inspired by true events of the 1920s, this timely thriller has resoundingly similar parallels to the contemporary war on terrorism.']

text:
The Jesse Owens story is one most Americans over the age of 50 know, some being far more knowledgeable than others. Race portrays Owens' trials and tribulations leading to the Berlin Olympics.

While the #1 reviewer said that "product knowledge" is a problem with this, I don't see it as such. Many years have elapsed and are now several generations removed from the original story and time. So, many watching it now would be learning firsthand of both Owens and the ultimate race of the races.

This is both a feel good and thought provoking movie and all parties involved did a great job of making it happen.
description: ['HD. The rise of Jesse Owens from college track-and-field superstar to Olympic legend, winning four gold medals in the 1936 Games.']

text:
Schlock. But okay schlock.
This 1930s Buck Rogers serial is much better quality than I have on DVD. Not only that but the audio is better and there are subtitles provided.
Married together from a series, this futuristic (yet, ancient) program has Buck Rogers and Buddy KO'd until the 25th century. (You won't be seeing starship Enterprise anywhere.)

What the 30s show the future to look isn't much further than their own time with Art Deco uniforms and architecture.

Hokey but fun.
description: ['An American soldier suspended in time wakes up to find himself in the futuristic world of the year 2500.']

text:
While Rupert Friend might be a good enough actor, he cannot fill Timothy Olyphant's shoes when it comes to being Agent 47.

In this installment of the Hitman series we find 47 trying to find and ultimately protect the daughter of the Agent program (Cieran Hind). The action is good and the choreography is very nice but Friend just doesn't make it. He's too personable.
description: ["HITMAN: AGENT 47, based on the popular video game, centers around the world's deadliest assassin – a genetically enhanced clone with superior intelligence and superhuman abilities!"]

title_x: You'll WANT to Watch This Film
text:
I have always like Ridley Scott's ideas of how things should be. In 1492: Conquest of Paradise, Scott imagines the New World as something new, exciting, exotic, strange and at the same time, peaceful, tranquil, and homelike.

Gérard Depardieu was wonderfully chose to portray Cristóbal Colón or Colombo or, as we are most apt to recognize the man, Christopher Columbus. It must have been a HUGE set of shoes for Mr. Depardieu to feel he must fill. Not only must he right the hundreds of years of myth but make the man a man. He was fantastic at it.

This is truly a magnificent movie. It's one that should be seen when there are no distractions. Have food and drink ready so as to not need to get up and leave. You'll WANT to watch this film.
description: ['This epic adventure and visionary film chronicles more than 20 years in the life of Christopher Columbus, one of the most celebrated, influential and mysterious men in history.']

text:
Harmonious Work. That's Gung Ho. Randolph Scott stars as the Raiders Colonel in this saga of the first offensive maneuverer in the Pacific.

description: ["The true story of Carlson's Raiders and their World War II attack on Makin Island."]

text:
Viking Saga was a dark, gray program. This is the English representation of the Northern invasion. The acting isn't that good but the story line is fairly decent.
This is the story of a young monk Hereward (Mark Pickering), who along with another monk escape the carnage of their monastery in Lindisfarne when it had been ransacked by Vikings. The two escape with the bible, or as Hadrada (Joshua Richards) calls it, the word of 'The White Christ'. They are bound for the refuge and safety of Iona.
Along the way they meet Aethelwulf (Mark Lewis Jones), a warrior of the ilk of Knights Templar. Aethelwulf ultimately gives his life to protect the Gospel of Lindisfarne as it makes its way to Iona.
title_y: A Viking Saga: The Darkest Day
description: ['A novice monk embarks on a mission to safely deliver a powerful holy book to a monastery. However a group of Vikings are in pursuit and will stop at nothing to get the book']

text:
My wife and I went into this movie exciting excitement, entertainment and, perhaps, amusement. This is the epitome of drama. If it isn't bad enought to be left for dead and return for revenge, the film makers felt it necessary to add components to the movie which really had no need being there. Those being the voice of a non-existant wife and the sidebar story of a son which defies facts of Glass' life.

This is an incredibly long movie clocking in at nearly 150 minutes You know how a movie speeds by when you're engrossed in it? Don't expect that to happen here. In fact, some of those minutes are painfully slow. Don't expect witty banter between characters. What dialog there is sounds as if the actors stuck a plug of chaw in their gobs before saying their lines.

Does all that mean it's not a good movie for others? Not at all. It just wasn't one for us.
description: ["Leonardo DiCaprio and Tom Hardy star in Alejandro G. Iñárritu's visceral, epic tale of survival and betrayal inspired by true events that's set in America's uncharted wilderness."]

text:

While off the street "The Pit" Bull is making a name by putting down his opponents "with extreme prejudice".

description: ["Bobby Delgado, undefeated MMA World Champion is incarcerated for eight years after accidentally killing his opponent. During this period of purgatory, Bobby experiences a paranormal 'life changing' event that will dictate his future path to redemption."]

title_x: 30 Years Later and Just as Good
text:
I know this got a bad rap from a lot of people. What I think is that those same people weren't around or barely even old enough to wipe themselves when the original movie came out. Tron: Legacy was a brilliant update/upgrade to the original '82 movie. Almost 30 years have passed and Flynn/Clu is still there.

text:
This is a fun movie. Yes, it's foul mouthed and there is a LOT of gratuitous violence but it's worth watching.

Three "trailer park" brothers, Brick (Clayne Crawford), McQueen (Travis Fimmel [[ASIN:B00CDTSFF8 Vikings]]), and the tall brother (6' 6") Lincoln (Daniel Cudmore) Oodie, known for their smash and kill tactics, are hired by Celeste (Eva Longoria) to retrieve a boy, Rob (Thomas Brodie-Sangster) from ex-husband Carlos (Billy Bob Thornton). text:

Oh, and you'll be happy to know Stegosaurus sound just like an elephant!

If, for some unknown reason, asked to watch this movie, grab yourself a BIG bag of potato chips, a bucket full of dip, a six pack of your favorite beverage and just empty your brain of thought and reason. text:
Citizen X is a wonderful drama. With Stephen Rea as Lt Viktor Burakov, a Medical Examiner tossed into the role of detective by a very stern Col Mikhail Fetisov (Donald Sutherland), Burakov is tasked with capturing a killer (Andrei Chikatilo (Jeffrey DeMunn), the Soviet Union's premier serial killer).

Blocked and redirected at every avenue by bureaucracy, mostly Comrade Bondarchuk (the outstanding Joss Ackland), the poor Burakov must do what he can with as little as possible. The feel of the movie is very like that of what we must felt the Soviet Union was like. Burakov must have been the Soviet Union's answer to [[ASIN:B008RJ6TTC Columbo]].

The amazing Max Von Sydow plays psychologist Dr. Alexandr Bukhanovsky, a man who feels it important to do what he does but worries it's not safe to practice psychology in the Soviet Union.

Released in 1995, the Soviet supremacy was still very much in our minds. This film has the feel of Arkady Renko from Martin Cruz Smith's 1983 [[ASIN:B00R1GI26A Gorky Park]].
description: ['A Russian police detective faces almost insurmountable odds in his search for the most savage serial killer of modern times.']

text:

Nathan (Oscar Isaac [[ASIN:B00VRE9W7K A Most Violent Year]]), his boss, a brilliant man in computers, has created artificial intelligence. Caleb is whisked off to Nathan's sprawling compound. Upon arrival Caleb is asked to sign "a typical NDA". After reading the non-disclosure agreement, Caleb remarks the agreement is anything but typical.

Caleb is introduced to Ava (Alicia Vikander). One of two primary AI's in the house. The other, Kyoko (Sonoya Mizuno) has no voice module. Caleb is supposed to figure out if Ava has a conscience/soul. He didn't actually win anything. He was chosen by Nathan.

I really wanted to enjoy this. Great idea, decent-ish script. What's not to like? It just seemed way too dry.

text:
If there's one thing I've learned from watching The Wire, patience pays. The Wire is a truly addictive show. My wife and I would get up an hour early to have our coffee in the morning and watch an episode before having to get things together for the day's events. Season 2 of The Wire centers on Baltimore's Harbor. Maj. Stanislaus Valchek (Al Brown) gets into a head butting contest with Stevedore Frank Sobotka (Chris Bauer) over what stained glass window will replace a broken one in their church. Because of this, Valchek tasks the Major Crimes Unit to get Sobotka based on money that shouldn't be available to him.

Season 2 only gets better with each episode. The first time I watched this series I wasn't very happy that it didn't center on the Barksdale crew. I was soon enthralled with what was going on. McNulty (Dominic West), relegated to the "boats" (Harbor Police), finds a body floating in the river. Using his talents to irritate any and everybody, he calculates the body had to have been dropped at a certain point ensuring the city's police department would catch the case. Subsequently, 13 women suffocate in a "can" (shipping container). Investigations reveal these woman were from the Russian Republics, smuggled in for purposes of prostitution.

Once the wire is up, the names start falling in place leading far further than anybody had expected. Great writing, fantastic acting make this one of the most captivating programs ever. Many new faces are introduced to this season including Ziggy Sobotka (James Ransome), Frank's son. Ziggy just can't catch a break. Anything he touches turns to s**t eventually leading to murder and the case coming to a nice clean, but not fully resolved, conclusion.
description: ['Season Two of the gritty HBO police drama takes on a new case involving unions on the Baltimore waterfront.']

title_x: A Very Fun Movie to Watch
text:
Jupiter Ascending is nothing life altering. You can miss this and still live a full life as a productive citizen. But, watch it and have fun knowing it's for your entertainment.

Jupiter Jones, daughter of an astronomer and mathematician from Russia. Jupiter's father was killed in a botched break in. Her mother, decidedly pregnant with Jupiter, joins a group being smuggled to the U.S. There she gives birth to Jupiter (named after her father's favorite planet).

Fast forward and we find Jupiter is the direct incarnation of an alien who happens to own Earth. Ownership of a planet assures both status and resources with resources including the inhabitants as a food source.

The story is fun. It's not necessarily new or original but the writers and actors managed to make the film refreshingly special.

This is a good Science-Fiction film. It's got all the elements of a movie you could go back and see again after a short time has elapsed.

This is a FUN movie. Watch it for that fun. It's not gross, terribly violent and the CGI is well done
description: ['From the streets of Chicago to far flung galaxies, Jupiter Jones embarks on an adventure as the next in line for an extraordinary inheritance that could alter the balance of the cosmos.']

William Hurt (who received an Oscar nod for Best Supporting Actor) plays Tom/Joey's brother Richie. Richie contacts Joey asking if he's coming to Philly or vice versa. From there this movie takes a very serious tack into the violence of the culture.

title_x: I Laughed and I Laughed and I Laughed Some More
text:
This really is a movie you need to take with a grain of salt. title_x: No Man Left Behind Still Means Something
text:
Okay, down with the naysayers. This is NOT the worst movie ever. It's far from it. It isn't bad at all. It IS predictable and it does use the same drone flyby over and over. And some scenes are better done than others, that's for sure.

Sector 4 is supposed to be that area between Afghanistan and Pakistan where the high level Taliban/Al Qaeda leaders cached themselves.

It's a basic movie about keeping promises of No Man Left Behind. Nash (Oliver Gruner, lead actor, director, producer and story writer) leads a four man squad to capture the #3 Most Wanted terrorist. Due to a lack of communications between the private contractors and military, Nash and his men are captured. Only Nash escapes, returns to the U.S. then vows to return to find his team.

This IS worth watching. It's entertaining and enjoyable. The action scenes are pretty good and for a B-movie, the camera work is decently done. If you're in the mood for a Buddy Flick, this could certainly hold its own.
description: ['An elite band of mercenaries is caught behind enemy lines and left for dead. When their mission leader escapes war-torn Sector 4, he pledges to return, leaving "No One Left Behind."']

title_x: Wyrmwood is Better than You Might Think

I was really surprised that I enjoyed Wyrmwood as much as I did. This was a "fun" zombie movie. Well, fun isn't really a word one should use with zombies. As one reviewer noted, this isn't Shawn of the Dead, a total laugh nor is Night of the Living Dead. This is "Whack-a-Mole" Zombie.

title_x: Brain Damage Makes This Movie Worth Watching
text:
This was probably the weirdest movie I've ever seen. Simon is looking for revenge. His daughter is killed in a mafia hit gone wrong. Simon becomes a hitman to find and execute the people responsible.

He is tasked with assassinating Gabby but spares her because she reminds him of his daughter and he also feels there's no compelling reason to do so. Carmine, mobdude, feels otherwise and when Simon didn't kill her puts out a on both Simon and Gabby.

The highlight of the movie, Brain Damage, is hired by Carmine. Brain Damage (who comes up with these names?) is basically dressed in Goth garb. His buddies are Fluffy, another winner, and Cancer. None of these characters are someone you'd want your daughter (or maybe even son) come home saying, "Hi, Dad. Meet my new boyfriend!"

The acting is borders on painful as if acting is brand new to each and every one of them. Gabby (Maya Juchtman) is REALLY rough around the edges as an actor. Everything is forced.

The actual highlight acting bit is performed by the character Brain Damage as he works what little magic there is in the entire movie.

title_x: An Uneven Movie with Action and Mickey Rourke
text:
Java Heat is an uneven movie. The main character, Jake (Kellen Lutz), is a man on a mission but we do not find out about his "mission" until he eventually tells his Javanese counterpart, Policeman LT "Hash" Hashim of Section 88.

Originally he tells Javanese police he is an Art Historian then he is found out. Hash tells Jake at one point, "Allah gave you two eyes and one mouth so that you can see twice as much as you speak."

The Sultana of Java is kidnapped but the kidnapping is masked in both a suicide bombing and her swapping by a hooker with the brand of a tiger. Ultimately, Hash's family is also kidnapped.

The ringleader of the whole thing is the Sultan's cousin the Vizier. He works with Malik (Mickey Rourke), a Frenchman?, and a very strange character indeed.

Action? This film has it. Intrigue? Loaded. Hot chicks? You know it. Great acting? No, they definitely missed the mark here.
description: ["Kellan Lutz ('Twilight') and Academy Award Nominee Mickey Rourke ('The Wrestler') star in an exotic cross-cultural action thriller about a reckless American who teams up with a Muslim cop to stop a terrorist mastermind."]

title_x: A Very Interesting Movie About Peace Through Terrorism and Revolution
text:
Having lived in the UK in the mid 70s through early 80s, I can vouch for the mindset of the "radicals," the skinheads and the like.

In the United States we don't quite have the same fear of annihalation as do we. During the Cold War the average missile from East Germany could reach the UK. The rest of Western Europe was an easy target.

Various radical groups throughout Europe and the UK attempted to thwart US, UK, FRG (W. Germany) and NATO efforts. This movie does an outstanding job conveying both the feel of the time and the problem.

There is some very exciting action and great acting. Yes, it does seem dated, because it is. But don't let the "bitchen music" and haircuts, especially for the supposed U.S. Air Force personnel fool you. That was sort of real for the times. (Not the Marines, though. They missed that one.) However, I am impressed that they fit the ribbons right.

This is an interesting movie. A radical group breaks in and holds the American ambassador residence hostage demanding the military fires a missile at Holy Loch, a Naval base known for housing U.S. submarines. The group wants to do that "in the name of peace". Richard Widmark's portrayal of the U.S. Secretary of State is brilliant.
description: ['Led by a radical chief, terrorists take over the American Embassy in London and make impossible demands that jeopardize the safety of the hostages.']

title_x: UHF is 90+ Minutes of Occasionally Funny Stuff

text:
Walking Dead's Season 5 may, to some, be the best ever. However, to this viewer it's the beginning of the great shark jump. The entire season seemed to be a hodge-podge of ideas. Who's right? Why is Rick always in charge? Doesn't it just annoy you the way he always leans in when he's going to talk? text:
By virtue of being a Godzilla movie this was an automatic, "Gotta check it out" film. By virtue of Jean Reno being in the movie, that's another "Gotta check it out" marker. Then there was Godzilla designer and supervisor Patrick Tatopoulos (Face Off series). With all this this should have been a grand slam

Matthew Broderick may not be one of the swiftest geese in the flock and adding Vicki Lewis (News Radio) to the mix didn't help matters much in making him look smarter. Kevin Dunn (Transformers) as the Colonel was one of the most unmilitary military characters ever. Michael Lerner (whose credits go back to '69) is one of the worst mayor characters in life. He would have fit in nicely in Animal House! In some ways this movie is just one joke after another and none were meant to be funny.

It seems nobody has a clue about the physics of flying either. Broderick's character is studying a specimen under a microscope in a storm inside a C-130. Now having NUMEROUS hours inside EP-3s and a lot of transit hours in 130s, I can assure you that specimen would not have stayed on the slide long enough to have looked at it much less look away and back to it again. Then let's take a gander at the fisherman who "catches" Godzilla in the b'day. That line would have snapped LONG before the pole was pulled from his hands.

Okay, back to the movie. Godzilla in New York? Why not! There's plenty to eat and loads of places to hide.
description: ["The enormous monster descends upon New York, and it's up to the Army and an odd team of investigators to unravel the mystery behind the incredible creature before it's too late."]

title_x: Season 5 Takes the Good and Makes it Great
text:
Season 5 reintroduces one of the best reoccurring characters on television ever - Castiel a/k/a Cass (Misha Collins). Cass is the Columbo of angels. There's never been a more stoic character that I can think of in 50 years of television viewing. He aids this series beyond anything I could ever hope for. Then there's the Prophet Chuck, or more simply Chuck Shurley (Rob Benedict). The writers were on a bender when they came up with this story line. Kurt Fuller plays Zachariah, one of the most obnoxious angels I've ever seen in my life. Mind you, I've not come across too many angels in my line of work.

title_x: ST: DS9 Season 6 Bids Adieu to LCDR Dax
text:

As always, the usual cast of the station kept themselves busy with the minutiae of daily life aboard a revolving "hotel" at the mouth of a wormhole. title_x: The Battle for Stalingrad Seen Through Both Sides
text:
One might think they were watching the wrong movie when this first begins. I know I had to double check to ensure I hadn't queued up the wrong one.

The story is told by the son of one resident survivor if the Battle for Stalingrad. Russian is dubbed into English and German is spoken in German. Subtitles DEFINITELY help although what is subtitled is not necessarily what was spoken.

Five Russian serviceman, four soldiers and one sailor are located in one of the many ruined multifloored buildings. One lone woman, the only survivor of the building remains. Eventually the soldiers (sailor included for brevity's sake) befriend the young woman.

On the other side of the town square and war are the encamped German soldiers. One Captain has taken up with a Russian girl. Although neither can understand each other's speech, they manage to carry on for some time. The Captain's boss, a Colonel, wants the Captain to (1) take the building where the Russians are and (2) have the Captain get rid of the Russian girl. Any action is only secondary to the drama with the exception of the German tanks which play a pivotal role in the movie.

This movie can sometimes be difficult to follow due to the conflicting between the dubbing and subtitles. Regardless of which language is being spoken, there is a love story happening in each side of the line.
description: ["Five Russian soldiers - and two women - hold their ground against the ruthless Nazi German army during the WWII's bloody, explosive Battle of Stalingrad. Spectacular wartime action! Subtitled."]

title_x: A Heart Wrenching Film of Courage and Valor
text:

Excellent acting from Denzel Washington, Morgan Freeman, Matthew Broderick, et al. The action was well shot and the directing by Edward Zwick (Last Samuraiand Defiance) was best perfect.

Sadly many Americans are unaware of the contributions of free black men during the Civil War. They fought galantly with valor and courage and truly did have more to lose than others.

Imagine a United States divided akin to North and South Korea or the former West and East Gemany. It was bad enough some families were
torn asunder, but this would have been a nation splintered.

title_x: Deadly Code is an Intense Movie About the Siberian Code
text:
A John Malkovich movie is already saying something ABOUT the movie - it's going to be odd. Deadly Code is no exception. Deadly Code is about four boyhood friends who were forced Siberian transplants during the Soviet Stalin era. The code by which they live is plain enough but when one crosses the line, to what ends must the code be upheld? This movie answers that question.

Kulyma, Gagarin (presumably because his real name was Yuri), Mel and Vitalic are the boyhood friends in question. Fast forward a decade and enter Xenya, a "gift from God". According to the Siberian code, "gifts from God" must be protected at all costs. Should something happen, then God must be appeased by the reprisal. Xenya falls for Kulyma and, it might seem, Gagarin. Kulyma is imprisoned and released after Grandfather Kuzya (John Maklovich) greases the appropriate palms. Only Kulyma's release comes at a price.

This is an intense movie. It you're not in the mood for drama, don't bother. You won't like it. If you have problems watching Malkovich, you might not like it.

text: I put off watching this show for a long time. Not sure why, perhaps because I couldn't picture Jeremy Pivon (sp?) staring in a PBS/Masterpiece Theater production. He created the modern department store in many ways. Of course this is also a drama so I think it is fair to say there is fiction and fictional characters mixed with facts here. Jeremy Piven really surprised me. I have never seen him in a drama and he pulls it off very well. Quite often when American actors get around British actors they tend to pick up a pretentious version of an English accent but he has managed to go through two seasons without that happening. Once you get hooked it is a very addictive show. It took me few episodes to really enjoy it and season two is much stronger than season one. The characters are more well rounded and more character's stories are being told. I think season one was a bit rushed at times. So much so that it was jarring. text:
I am stunned that this show was cancelled. I personally believe this show is another example of how the ratings system used by the networks is completely broken. I don't even remember that this show was telecast, but thanks to Amazon Prime, I have been watching and enjoying the series immensely.

The acting, directing, and character development is superb. I have to admit that I initially hated the first episode because of the characters. But that was more my own perception problems. I thought the characters were poor because they didn't behave the way that I think they should in an apocalypse. I then realized that the writers had it right much more than me. The show has a mixture of a no nonsense mayor, to his political opponent that undermines him at every opportunity, to the mayors delinquent son with a mysterious past, his hot ex-girlfriend who's engaged to someone else, etc. A lot of complex characters and relationships. The town, itself, goes through the various stages of trauma, shock, denial, anger, grief, acceptance. The transition isn't pushed and the development occurs at the right pace so that the audience gets to know all the characters but it's not drawn out so that you lose interest. If there is one criticism, it's on the overall story arc. I'm almost half way through the season and you still don't know what is going on outside the town. I think they could have developed that part of the story a lot more.

If you like The Walking Dead or Revolution, you will enjoy this show. The characters and acting is just as good as Dead with a storyline similar to Revolution but without all the graphic violence. But be warned, the show is addicting. I watched the first 9 episodes in a 48 hour period.

text: I read a lot of the reviews and criticisms of the movie and while I can agree that they have technical merit, they were not sufficient to prevent me from enjoying the experience. Yes, the characters were not thoroughly fleshed out or sympathetic but how much insight into their inner worlds should you expect from found footage covering a couple of days? The first movie thoroughly unsettled me for weeks (given that I had just moved into a house in the woods) and this one did not have the same impact. I credit that to the novelty of the original combined with the auxiliary material on the web and supporting "documentary" tv shows. I felt this sequel achieved a good percentage of its potential while remaining true to the mythology of the original and extending it without undoing it. I rented this movie and watched it, read people's opinions of it, then watched it again. Still enjoyed it the second time so take that for what it's worth. If you want a new experience that has the sledgehammer impact of The Blair Witch Project, watch The Witch. If you want to revisit the experience of the original and see its world from a more modern perspective, Blair Witch 2016 is what you have available, and you could do a lot worse.

UPDATE - April 8, 2013: I just wanted to take a moment to remember the real Margaret Thatcher, who died today. She was a great lady and I do hope that her strength, integrity and huge contributions to history will be remembered truthfully and fairly.

I so agree with what Senate Republican Leader Mitch McConnell said regarding the senate resolution honoring Lady Thatcher, "Let me just say that Margaret was one of the most influential and revolutionary figures of the 20th century, and failing to name her achievements would do her memory and her legacy a great disservice. It would be unheard of to commemorate Churchill for example and ignore his heroic role in steering his countrymen through the battle of Britain, nor would we think of honoring Lincoln without mentioning the Civil War," McConnell said. He added: "Let's acknowledge the enormity of what she accomplished. Let's mention her achievements by name and the resolution does that because we owe her a tribute equal to her legacy."

Truer words were never spoken, and this sentiment very aptly applies to the movie THE IRON LADY. May she Rest In Peace. ~Linda~

ORIGINAL REVIEW - April 15, 2012: I cannot understand what they were thinking! An opportunity to make a movie about one of the MOST FASCINATING AND INFLUENTIAL WOMEN OF THE TWENTIETH CENTURY. The greatest actress of our generation playing the lead. And this opportunity is squandered on a ditzy, artsy-fartsy script that examines the whole thing through the fictional fantasy lens of and elderly Margaret Thatcher's demented flashbacks - as if anyone actually knows what is really going on in the mind of a person with dementia. What a waste.

It started out OK. A lot of movies detailing the lives of great people start out in the first 10 minutes showing the main character in advanced old age and the main story is told in a long flashback. This kind of plot device was done very well in the movie "Chariots of Fire". I don't mind knowing that Margaret Thatcher is suffering from dementia - it is a fact and is not out of place in a story about her life. But the problem with "The Iron Lady" is that the story got stuck in the advanced old age segment and about 45 minutes into the movie, I realized that the makers of this bomb had no intention of examining the MAIN STORY at all. The WHOLE thing was about a lonely, demented old woman whose glory days have passed her by and now she is of no importance. I found myself heaving an involuntary sigh of exasperation when I was subjected to yet another imaginary conversation held in the "fictional" Mrs. Thatcher's hallucination world. What little factual and historically relevant information they included was hazy and spotty. The flow of the script is so disjointed that no sensible understanding of Margaret Thatcher's incredible life, accomplishments, family, or career can be gleaned from this self indulgent mess. The people involved in making this boring, pointless movie should be ashamed. I was expecting so much because it could have been great but was sorely disappointed.

A flick about an elderly woman suffering from dementia should have been saved for an arthouse fiction about dementia, not imposed on a life story of someone of this magnitude. Really, what could have been the motive for obsuring Margaret Thatcher's enormous contributions to the twentieth century? Could it be that the makers of this flick hated her and her politics and wanted to diminish and marginalize her but didn't have the courage to do it in an honest and up front fashion? That is the only thing I can figure out because this movie makes absolutely no sense at all. At best, it is a tawdry invasion of Mrs. Thatcher's and her family's privacy as she faces a slow and difficult death. Perhaps it is a fact that she is struggling with dementia, but the writers of this script are not privy to the details of how that is being played out and have been forced to fictionalize it to an absurd degree in order to have a story that leaves out who she really is. To magnify this small aspect of her life while brushing aside the bulk of her life's work is almost criminal.

There are only three good things that I have to say about this movie. First, the make up artist did an exceptional job of making Meryl Streep look extremely elderly. Most of the time, old age make up is sloppy and not believable, but I have to say that Ms. Streep really did look realisticly old in this movie. The second thing is that Meryl Streep did a great job of acting, as usual. It is a pity that she has no better judgement than to lend her great talent to a substandard production like this one. I have always had some respect for Ms. Streep, but after watching this movie, I have lost some of my former good opinion of her. The third thing was that the movie finally ended and I never have to see it again.

I will never get back the time and money I wasted watching this stupid show, but I can spare just a few extra minutes to warn you that this is a waste of time for anyone who wishes to actually know anything about Margaret Thatcher and her real life. Those facts are documented for anyone to see and no story teller needs to descend into outrageous liscence to make a movie with something worthwhile to say. If you want to make a moive about dementia, then make a movie about dementia. If you want to make a movie about Margaret Thatcher, then please, PLEASE make a true one.

text:
We really enjoy Miss Spider's Sunny Patch, but I think I might enjoy it more than my daughter. I loved the book, Miss Spider's Tea Party, and so did my daughter. We love pretending to be a mommy spider and baby spider, so I thought she would enjoy this show. She's 3 so I think maybe she doesn't 'get' some of the points the show is trying to make, which maybe is why it's not as enjoyable for her yet. I think the best age group might be ages 4-9.

Animation is very bright and colorful and there's a lot going on, so it's not very soothing. But it's not annoying like many other kid's shows. It's cute so it probably won't get in your nerves to watch with your kids. The animation and colors are so intense I find it difficult to watch for long, but I can see how this is appealing to children. You have to do a lot to catch their attention sometimes.

Perfect for adoptive families, since almost all of Miss Spider's kids are adopted! LOVE seeing this represented in kids' programming. Both Miss Spider and the kids are very frank and sweet about their adoptive family unit, so refreshing!

text: What a wonderful documentary! It was so much fun being drawn into the mystery of a Shakespearean code (with ties to Masonic and Rosicrucian elements). I am not a person who is invested in a certain view about whether or not Shakespeare was the "True" author of his works, so I wasn't bothered by the chase...it was exciting to imagine the possibilities inherent in the books. Robert Crumpton was fun to watch because he so clearly IS invested in Shakespeare being the true author, and he was red-faced and angry several times. (I thought he was going to bust out into a full tantrum at one point!)  Petter Amundsen was a very authentic, calm and intelligent person throughout the documentary. Clearly he is passionate about his search for the "truth", but you never get the sense that he is some kind of fanatic. The fact that one of the world's most esteemed code-breakers says there absolutely IS a code in Shakspeare's works is hard to ignore. Regardless of what your personal opinion is about Shakespeare, the Masons and the Rosicrucians, watching this film is like going on a roller-coaster ride. If you got a kick out of watching The DaVinci Code, you will most likely love this one!

title_x: A fantastic movie for giant robot fans
text:
Malinger Z Infinity is a gorgeous, stunning animated movie. A Whirlwing of Action and character moments. It starts off running and rarely slows down (except for a few oh so anime whiny brooding moments.) Viz’s English dub is rather surprisingly good. I would go so far as to call it fantastic as far as anime dubs go. (Thank god it wasn’t Funimation)

Now the cautionary bit. Malinger Z Infinity is a love letter to the deep Mazinger universe and properties. It is a climax. A look at old friends that you haven’t seen in years. This is not a great jumping on point for Mazinger lore and characters. It is the oh so satisfying conclusion. The movie hits the ground running, and at no point does it stop to bring newcomers up to speed. This is the animated equivalent to Avengers Infinity War, and just as walking into that with no prior knowledge of the MCU will leave one baffled, so will walking into this cold. At least some knowledge of the core Mazinger Z and Great Mazinger stories and characters is needed. Particularly Mazinger Z vs the Great Dark General. At a minimum pull up a Wikipedia entry and learn a little of the story and characters before diving into this one. Just a little bit of prior knowledge will make this much more enjoyable.

The animation is a whirlwind of cell shaded CGI. Which isn’t quite as suspension of disbelief breaking as such things normally are.

The story is set several years after the events of the mainline Mazinger Z and Great Mazinger stories. Our well known characters have grown up, matured and largely begun non robot lives. The technology that created the Mazingers has transformed the world, providing near unlimited stable clean energy. When a new Mazinger is found, and the great evil returns.

The movie introduces a new character, who at times feels jarring ly out of place. Because no giant robot is allowed to not have a blue haired Rei Ayanami clone Waifu character anymore. I will give credit that they do take an annoying and cliched 90’s-00’s type new character, that seems out of place in the 70’s era Mazinger property, and somehow make it work by the end. The final realization of who the new character is, or rather will be makes up for the earlier annoyance. (Think Ashoka Tano from the Star Wars Cline Wars tv series. From her horrifying introduction, until her exit as the one character that rivals Luke Skywalker in fan popularity.)

Overall this is a great watch for fans of classic robot shows. It’s a deep love letter to everything that went before. But it does require some familiarity with the property to fully enjoy.
description: ['Ten years after the defeat of Dr. Hell and his Underground Empire, Koji Kabuto has retired from piloting Mazinger Z and become a scientist. Now a shocking discovery under Mt. Fuji has revealed the greatest threat the Earth has ever known, forcing Koji and his friends to once again fight for the future of all humanity.']

title_x: At least it is a little better than the unextended version? Yeah for the hardcore fans and completionists.
text:
And so we come to the Misty Mountains at long last. long long last. Even longer last. Did I mention long? Overall all 3 Hobbit movies are reasonably good, but suffer from too much of a good thing and would have worked better being edited to two. There are some great pieces in this movie. Plus a good number that will leave Tolkien fans scratching their heads going WTF??? Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings these movies are not. Deeply ruined by the inclusion of tons of extraneous characters that never appeared in the original story. The hot Elf on Dwarf romance was kinda odd. The Dwarbes fighting the dragon was certainly unexpected as well as being rather idiotic and long.

The best part of the Extended edition is it put back in some critical scenes that really should have been left in to begin with. I mean they actually explain why Thranduil is such a jackass. But they cut the needed story and exposition in favor of an extra 10 minutes of idiotic dwarves in barrels like some amusement park ride. Someone really needs to explain to Peter Jackson the difference between using a feather and using the whole damn chicken.

For Tolkien and LotR fans it is pretty much a must see in order to get to the end of it all. And the extended edition is the better cut. But if you haven't seen The Unexpected Journey this will make no sense to you. If you saw the prior movie but also read the book, this will make even less sense to you. Probably just best to forget that it has anything to do with JRR Tolkien and convince yourselves that this is the best Dungeons & Dragons movie ever made. Your soul will die a little less that way.

title_x: Slice of life approach works in this film's favor
text: There seem to be two camps of opinions on Boyhood, at least among my friends and acquaintances. Some hail it as a brilliant and groundbreaking film, others point out that the whole thing is just a series of events without a conventional plot or other dramatic devices that hold viewer attention. While the latter has some validity, I found the film to be more interesting for its slice-of-life approach. This is a movie where you really don't know what's going to happen next, and where dramatic tension builds from just a few shots or lines of dialog. It all feels very real in a way that more traditional films about some of the same subject matter sometimes don't. Nothing feels forced or contrived to this viewer. To me, this is the mark of success for this filmmaker and cast. Big experiments don't always turn out successfully in film or other artistic areas, but when they do it's a great thing. I really enjoyed this experience and recommend it.

text: Downton Abbey never disappoints. The story line is compelling, the acting superb, and the characters are well-developed. Every time an episode ends, my husband and I are left wanting more. Sometimes evil versus good is painted a bit too black and white and needs a bit of gray; many humans who are selfish or sly or demanding or self-willed can also do something unselfish or kind occasionally. Some can also find through self-examination how to end the self-inflicted wounds, which come from self-seeking thoughts and actions, and thus become better people. I like the show's willingness to have characters grow and change, but a couple characters do seem to remain evil personified. Overall, I recommend the show as a good study in human nature, a grand view of a bygone era, and an entertaining story.

Silence of the Lambs is fascinating because we get to watch a rookie try to stay on to of someone she knew was leagues ahead of her. The plot and writing are spot on, and you can tell that all the actors devote as much as possible to the roles. Edward Norton is wonderful as Will Graham, and it's always a ball seeing Anthony Hopkins play Hannibal.

text:
On the surface this is a great movie: it's beautiful and artful.

As a transgender individual myself, it was interesting to watch the life of this Danish girl as she figures out that she's transgender. Eddie Redmayne (Einar/Lili) does a great job at displaying dysphoria and some of the struggles of feeling trapped in the wrong body! There is a scene where Lili runs to a theater and undresses in front of a mirror and tucks her appendage between her legs so that she can see what she'd look like without it. OMG!! I can relate to this so much! (this is the ONLY reason I gave the movie two stars). Someone really did their research or has actual experience in that regard.

Here's my problem: the movie was recommended to me by a coworker who knows that I am transgender. There was a "two person" element of the Danish Girl's character that is off putting. Her wife BEGS her to go get Einar (the husband) and Lili refuses to do so. The direction made is seem like the Danish Girl had Dissociative Identity Disorder (Multiple Personality Disorder): As if the Lili and was simply an alter and that they switched from one to the other. This is NOT what it means to be transgender and I found it to be a little offensive. Now, I'm concerned that my coworker thinks this is what has happened with me.

At first, I liked the movie for its portrayal of the spouse's struggle (which was strikingly similar to what my own spouse went through). However, the longer I thought about the movie the more I began to despise it. Others may feel differently about how transgenderism is displayed but I don't think I can recommend this movie to anyone I know who isn't partially woke: my own mother would get the wrong idea about transgender individuals if she watched this movie.
