In fact, the plot is silly at times, with people making obviously stupid choices as to who to be with, but don’t worry it all turns out for the best at the end, as it always will in a film like this.  The predictability is not a bad thing here, it just adds to its entertainment movie.  So if you are looking for something that will remind you of a summer you may never have had but wish you did, this will be just the ticket.
description: ['It’s the summer of 1982 on Long Island and life is good. JJ is working at the Beach Club, when he falls for Debbie. Frankie reconnects with a long lost love. But as temperatures cool, so do their relationships, leaving them to accept summer is ending.']

title_x: good live reproduction of an action comic
text: Clearly a comic book, in live action, in all respects.  The outlandish action sequences, the one-dimensional characters, the failure of even severe injuries to affect the good guys, the physics-defying effects (like bullets moving in curved trajectories), the rapid turn around from a supreme nebbish into a hero of the galaxy.  But despite it all, the film is lots of fun, in the same way you can get a guilty pleasure from a good action comic.  Acting?  Well, no real acting to speak of.  No characters to develop.  But it all fits together into a fun couple hours.
description: ['James McAvoy, Morgan Freeman and Angelina Jolie star in Wanted, a turbo-charged thrill ride critics are calling the most visually inventive, trailblazing action film of its kind.']

title_x: try to not get into the details - just enjoy the scenes for what they are
text: Well, I am not sure what I just watched.  But if I’m honest I would have to admit I kind of liked it.  The overall plot is incoherent.  It is more like a few odd scenes pasted together.  The sean penn scene, augmented by tom waits was hilarious.  And the brad cooper character is simply hilarious.  What they had to do with the storyline is questionable.  In fact the film is at its best when it simply abandons the quasi romance between the two leads and focuses on the auxiliary characters.  So watch, and no, you are not misunderstanding the story line.  It is a tenuous one.
description: ['The story of Alana Kane and Gary Valentine growing up, running around and falling in love in the San Fernando Valley in 1973.']

title_x: some strong points diluted by unexplained silence of main character
text: Has some good seeds, some good ideas.  Talks about what it might be like to grow up in a family of this sort.  With so much emphasis on the family religion.  And with an overbearing father to whom this religion is his entire identity (note they never told us anything else about him).  So it was educational, and we can see parallels in people growing up in any other fundamentalist group.  But the script had some problems too.  Tariq was far too hostile - to EVERYONE.  And he was so reluctant to say anything.  Why could he not tell anyone about the physical abuse?  Why would he not explain his position to his roommate, his friend cedric, or the girl that showed interest in him?  Made the entire film a little too frustrating.
description: ["Amid a strict Muslim rearing and a social life he's never had, Tariq enters college confused. New peers, family and mentors help him find his place, but the 9-11 attacks force him to face his past and make the biggest decisions of his life."]

title_x: the premise is far from credible
text: Has some redeeming features, but the underlying concept is not credible.  That an ex would invite a current wife, and her kid, to move in with her and her daughter was preposterous.  Even if depleted of funds, that the current wife would agree is also ludicrous.  OK, so let’s buy the premise.  The daughter of the ex is just too obnoxious at every turn, beyond simply acting out her age. And are we to believe that the ex is so fabulously wealthy, and that her ex-husband was so inconsiderate as to leave his current family destitute, with no hint of that?  So, no, just can’t buy much of this film.
description: ["A divorced mother and her daughter must contend with living in the same house as the ex-husband's second wife and daughter following his unexpected death."]

title_x: interesting twist on a road trip film
text: The basic idea of an estranged brother/sister getting to know each other on a road trip sounds trite.  But this one has enough interesting dialogue, a few quirky characters, and some twists to make it engaging.  And both lead actors are quite good, likable, and you hope they can work through their issues.  You watch as they unwind their old relationships, and hope they can really connect again (spoiler alert: they do).  The ending was a little weak, poorly thought out plot design, needlessly running around.  But that was a minor weakness, as the basic story and characters carry the whole thing.
description: ["After their mother passes, dysfunctional siblings Star and Brandon are forced to confront their issues and their broken relationship as they carry out their mother's final wish: a road trip to a Texas aquarium to spread her ashes."]

text: Between the music, the scenery, the quiet, we get a unique atmosphere that carries the film.  You know early on, not  just because of the title, that the tracker is to be the key character here.  The so-called fanatic is just that, and a symbol for white racism, oppression, and violence throughout the world.  If there is a weakness in the film it is that he is too symbolic, not really a person.  He is so evil, and needlessly violent, that you cannot wish him anything good at all, (spoiler alert) so his end is more than justified.  The younger man is perhaps symbolic of what white people could be if they would only let go of their many hatreds and prejudices.  A fine film on many levels.
description: ["It's 1922; somewhere in Australia. When a Native Australian man is accused of murdering a white woman, three white men are given the mission of capturing him with the help of an experienced Native Australian. So they start their quest in the outback, not knowing that their inner wrestles against and for racism will be more dangerous that the actual hunting for the accused."]

title_x: not what you might expect from the blurb
text: Unusual casting.  The hitman did not fit any typical film stereotype of a hitman.  Sort of tall and gangly, and awkward, not self-assured by any measure.  The instant rapport between him and the girl was just too quick, love at first sight, with no conversation whatsoever.  And the fact that she could find his stashed cash so easily makes you wonder.  But even with all that (or maybe because of it0, this was an enjoyable film, despite all the gore from time to time.  To like this, you will have to look past some of the holes in the plot, and the gratuitous violence.  One more thing: the soundtrack of indie music is like another cast member, and discussed quite a bit.
description: ['Max, a hitman working in Los Angeles, meets one of his targets, Karen. When Max hears Karen sing, he feels compelled to spare her life. They fall in love, and Max realizes he needs one last job before they can leave town together.']

title_x: good but a little light on character development
text: Maybe not as engaging as it might have been.  There was not enough fleshing out of the characters.  But it was a pretty good film, gave you a firsthand account of the development of nuclear weapons.  From the perspective of a Polish immigrant mathematician, and his compatriots, most of whom were also immigrants.  Would have liked a bit more meat on the events as well as his personal life, but overall a worthwhile film.
description: ['The warmhearted story of Polish immigrant and mathematician Stan Ulam, who moved to the U.S. in the 1930s. Stan deals with the difficult losses of family and friends all while helping to create the hydrogen bomb and the first computer.']

title_x: amusing remake of the old In Living Color TV show
text: The flavor is in the same vein as the old tv show In Living Color, including some of the Wayans brothers.  Almost like a series of skits stitched together.  They even did a remake of the old TV sketch of the black movie critics, although here they were not gay.  The skits are rather amusing, a view of white people and movie culture from the standpoint of black people in America.  Reminds us of the stereotypes that these films foster not just of blacks, but of Asians and other minorities, and even of women.  No real plot per se, but rather entertaining.
description: ['Bobby Taylor is an aspiring actor and hot-dog stand employee who dreams of making it big. Cast in an exploitation film full of racial stereotypes, he falls into a series of daydreams satirizing the typecasting black actors face in Hollywood.']

text: There is no central plot here.  Rather we just visit with various denizens of a small provincial town in Italy with short bursts, then move on to the next group.  We observe all sorts of relationships, the most central of which is the yearning of the young men to move on to bigger and better things, only to be pulled back by the gravity of their hometown.  There are no deep revelations here about human relations, nor profound truths exposed.  More like what a tourist would see if allowed to listen in on conversations.  Amusing, entertaining, but also kind of shallow.  Probably the sort of film to watch if you are also engaged in some other activities, a sort of background.
description: ["Three young men, live in a small, poverty-stricken village. Since they are all unemployed, they while their time away roaming the streets and chasing girls. One day, Antonio's aunt asks him to follow her and his cousins in Rome. He accepts her offer and enrolls at a university in Rome, leaving his two friends behind. Honorary Oscar's Award winner Lina Wertmüller's stunning debut film."]

title_x: excellent spy suspense film with some new twists
text: be prepared for a bit of a roller coaster ride, as you oscillate between confidence in their success, anxiety that they will be caught, and back and forth.  cumberbatch has an opportunity to show off his considerable acting skills, which takes him from an innocent and naive businessman to a dedicated spy, and dealing with personal and family issues along the way.  brosnahan was not a great choice - she is the least convincing of the cast.  excellent film that keeps you on the edge of your seat nearly from beginning to end, without need of guns and car chases.
description: ['Benedict Cumberbatch (DOCTOR STRANGE) and Rachel Brosnahan ("The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel") star in this true-life Cold War spy thriller about British businessman Greville Wynne, who must form an alliance with a Soviet spy to prevent a nuclear confrontation.']

title_x: intelligently written dialogue, makes you think
text: what a nice surprise.  thought when they talked about rap in the blurb that it would be all style and no substance.  but quite the opposite.  very well written dialogue, which was in fact the focus of this one.  touches on a number of issues: life, meaning of life, relationships, racism.  i was impressed with the writer, who was not a bad director either.  well worth a watch - and a listen.
description: ['A young rapper moves to Los Angeles in search of stardom and instead finds an unlikely friend in his dispirited apartment manager whose dreams led him to the same city twenty years prior.']

text: a superficial script, complemented by terrible acting.  the story is silly.  the heart of the trauma is that a boy was gay.  that he was caught kissing another boy in a locker room.  this caused his father to hate him, until he returns and helps is father win a bowling tournament (!?)  and the two of them wind up in a fistfight with some bullies (!?).  and the sean character is supposed to be drop-dead gorgeous but the actor is quite plain (and forgot to shave).  the revelation at the end is anything but.  underwhelming.
description: ['Sean (Adrian Grenier) takes us on a powerful and emotional journey to learn that the secret to life is loving what you have. Sean now a successful fashion designer returns to his hometown for a painstaking family reunion that will take him back to his past, only to rebuild his future.']

text: yes, the script was pretty silly, and yes the characters did not act like real people, and the "science" had more holes than the space-time continuum.  and the acting was pretty bad.  but actually it was still a lot of fun. it is one of those films where you just have to forget about reality and just sit back and enjoy it.  so overall, worth a viewing if you know what you are getting.
description: ["A struggling scientist has a UFO encounter that turns his world upside down. Fate guides him to meet a quirky female artist and he begins to fall in love, never suspecting she's the alien from the UFO."]

text: a true indy in a number of ways.  there is no plot, per se.  we just follow around a young woman for a couple of days as she tries to cope with the loss of her father.  she does so in a promiscuous and drug-addled way, so we try to understand her behavior. there are a few comical characters, her friend, her boss, her roommate, that add a bit of spice to what would otherwise be a sad character study.  the acting is surprisingly good for such a low-budget affair.  well worth a watch.
description: ['After the sudden death of her distant father, a young woman copes by distracting herself with alcohol, drugs, and the antics of her misguided friends.']

text: combines teen angst/puppy love with . . . . a nuclear apocalypse.  yes you heard that right.  the "war" makes no sense.  who are these enemies, these so-called terrorists?  they can invade the UK so easily?  and why do they bomb civilian targets?  why do they bother chasing civilians around, and kill them for no reason?  why do the UK army units treat their own citizens like POWs?  what is the point of walking for a week with no food or water to return to a bombed out house, also with no food or water?  comes off more like a video than a coherent movie.  sorry, just a bomb (pun intended)
description: ['Set in the near-future UK, Saoirse Ronan plays Daisy, an American teenager sent to stay with relatives in the English countryside. Initially withdrawn and alienated, she begins to warm up to her charming surroundings and strikes up a romance with the handsome Edmund (George MacKay). But on the fringes of their idyllic summer days are tense news reports of an escalating conflict in Europe. As the UK falls into a violent, chaotic military state, Daisy finds herself hiding and fighting to survive.']

title_x: silly fun - and lots of it
text: just silly fun. the plot is about as complicated as any of the beach blanket movies.  some of the dancing is quite good.  the acting quality is irrelevant for such an inane plot; likewise for the script.  but after all is said and done, it is fun to watch these people going through the motions, what with the singing and dancing.  also fun to see what must have been one of the earliest film roles of helen hunt and parker, the sex and city lady.  if you watch this, you will know exactly what to expect.
title_y: Girls Just Want to Have Fun
description: ["Sarah Jessica Parker, Helen Hunt and Shannen Doherty star in the outrageous '80s comedy hit that's totally packed with outrageous '80s fashions, music, dance moves, and more!"]

title_x: suspense coupled with coming of age
text: a suspense film of a sort, but one that has a large piece dealing with the coming of age of an adolescent.  also strong elements of how a child deals with the disappearance of a parent.  you are sucked into her life, and watch as she grows up, emotionally, intellectually, and sexually.  but there is always the lingering question of why and where her mom had gone.  until the very very end, with a great surprise that nobody saw coming.  quite a good little film, with suspense and also interest in her life.
description: ["Kat Connors' (Shailene Woodley) glamorous but strange mother Eve (Eva Green) vanishes. Kat is excited by her new freedom, distracted by the boy next door and the cop working the case. Disturbing facts surface and the mystery begins to haunt her."]

text: a senseless script, with little meaningful dialogue, a central character whose motivations are a mystery, a relationship that petered out for no understandable reason, and is flaring up again even though there is no chemistry between the two leads.  couple that with very bad acting, and by highly amateurish directing.  what am i forgetting?  oh yeah, a lead actress with a permanent scowl on her face.
description: ['An actress confronts her quarter-life crisis by breaking up with New York City and returning home to win back the love of her life.']

title_x: overly ambitious to the point of confusion
text: nicely photographed, and with a nice flavor about it.  a story about a family that has to change with the times and accept some of the loss that comes with that, a feeling of loss.  the problem with the film though is that it is hard to understand what people are doing and why.  the heart of the film is the developing relationship between the middle aged woman and the young chef.  but there is zero development of this.  they don't even talk to each other before getting uber passionate.  so you never understand what she is gaining or losing.  the dreams they show have no connection to anything i could figure out.  almost like the director is trying (badly) to emulate fellini.  not an awful film, but leaves you dissatisfied, empty at the end.
description: ["At the heart of the wealthy Recchi family is Tancredi Recchi's wife Emma (Tilda Swinton), whose existence is shocked to the core when she embarks on a passionate love affair that will change her family forever."]

text: this was awful.  could not even get through it.  cardboard cutout characters, some no more than cartoons of real people.  the kids behavior make no sense, nor can we figure out the father's behavior.  or the guy that runs the music store.  just a hot steaming mess.
description: ['A family embarks on an adventure inspired by a bucket list made many years ago and are able to move forward and manage their grief after a terrible loss.']

text: just a slight cut above a hallmark movie.  on the positive side, you tend to like the characters and feel their losses when they occur.  but with the single exception of an ineffectual bully kid, there is absolutely nobody who isn't perfect.  all good intentions, everyone likes each other, there is never the slightest hint of physical discipline on the kids, even the great grandma is a nice lady.  just strains credulity - hey if there is such a place, i am moving there tomorrow.  and the rift between the two girls is artificial, and even though she has stayed away for years, all it takes is a quick little apology and it is all lovey dovey again.
description: ["In 1967, two sisters, Juliet (Darby Camp) and Evangeline (Chandler Head) are abandoned and raised by grandparents Walt (Corbin Bernsen) and Ruby (Melissa Gilbert) in the town of Fireside. Walt's eccentric mother Itasca (Cloris Leachman), adds laughter and tears. Humor, heartbreak and triumph are served with whipped cream and lots of local nuts in this tale of family, friendship and forgiveness."]

text: the idea had some potential, but the characters were just too over the top.  i am not gay but i imagine gay people would be offended by the overdone stereotypes here.  the story is too simple to carry a full-length feature film.  the ending was just not very well thought out either.
description: ["Ricky Redmond is a teen acting legend--at least in his own mind (and his mother's, of course). He's confident that he's a shoe-in for the leading role his senior year. That is, until Josh Kelly, the school's star baseball player, surprises everyone and auditions. The claws come out as a vicious battle for the spotlight ensues."]

text: what started out as an intriguing crime drama devolved into such a convoluted plot that no sense could be made of it.  did the scene we just saw really take place?  are we supposed to replace one character by another?  who gets shot after all?  and all the silly rambo style shooting and explosions made it seem like a cheap knockoff.  very disappointing.
description: ['The Hong Kong police are hunting a counterfeiting gang led by a mastermind code-named "Painter". In order to crack the true identity of him, the police recruits gang member Lee Man to unmask "Painter\'s" secret identity.']

text: excellent on a number of levels.  first there is the personal story of the meteoric rise of a young man from abject poverty to corporate superstar.  mixed in with this is the fact that he is half chinese and half british, a real handicap in the social structure in which he was raised.  a story of family bonds as well, unshakable no matter what.  and a romance that simmers below the surface as our hero never learned how to display emotion.  the backdrop for it all is the bubbling cauldron of hong kong: british imperialism, chinese nationalism, thirst for wealth, all brewed together.  this film is both touching and enlightening, emotional yet educational.  truly excellent film-making.
description: ['In 1940s Hong Kong, an orphaned boy rises above oppressive circumstances to become an esteemed engineer for the British colonies, but still struggles to learn where he came from. From legendary director Yim Ho comes a lyrical and heartbreaking story of family, identity and love that survives generations.']

text: tries too hard to be edgy, cultish, overly cute.  the two leads spend the entire film in pink bunny outfits for no good reason.  one of them tries to be crude, smoking, drinking, cursing, but that only goes so far.  the supporting characters serve no particular function, and behave beyond odd.  occasionally a little amusing, but mainly just tedious.
description: ['Two blue-collar Easter Bunnies get fired and try their hand at an assortment of odd jobs, failing at each.']

title_x: one of the better films about ww1
text: a sprawling film that documents the effects of WW1 on one particular young woman at what should be the high point of her life.  brings home the horrors of war, not only to the soldiers but to their families and loved ones.  vikander is terrific in her role: charming, charismatic, yet also hard and ambitious.  she brings all these feelings and emotions to the screen so a viewer can experience them all along with her.  along with her, we feel the young love, the burning ambition, the promise of a life, all cut short as one after another of her loved ones die off.  the cinematography is first rate.  the film does not seem as long as it is, due to the excellent script, pacing, and acting.
description: ['During World War I, Oxford University student Vera Brittain postpones her studies to serve as a nurse while her suitor, her brother, and a secret admirer face death in the trenches.']

description: ['Fighting for the survival of the entire world, the Protagonist journeys through a twilight world of international espionage on a mission that will unfold in something beyond real time.']

text: all about the developing relationship between sam and ben that begins with a drive up the Cal highway from LA.  some nice views of scenery along the way that is integral to the film, so credit to cinematographer.  the conversations are interesting in the first half, but deteriorates when they introduce other characters, like a hitchhiker and an older couple.  then it just seems forced and kinda silly.  it is difficult to understand sam's behavior toward the end as she seems to want to end the relationship for no reason.  a film like this depends heavily on a chemistry between the two leads which was ok but not great.

Ben (Scott Keiji Takeda) and Sam (Hannah Leigh) take to the iconic Pacific Coast Highway and realize that the farther they drive, the closer they grow, and those forces that kept them looking back are being left far behind.']

title_y: Charade - Cary Grant, Audrey Hepburn, Uncut Suspense Classic!

When the boy chases a dog into the woods and gets lost, he must use the magic taught to him by the clown to find his way home. text: feels as though some hollywood moguls decided it would be boffo box office to get sinatra and crosby together in a film with kelly.  only problem is they had no script for them.  so they just threw some crap together, something about the idle rich being not so bad, and writers for a tabloid being not so bad.  then they got cole porter to write some of the worst songs of his career so they could toss in his name as well.  throw in louis armstrong.  got the names.  can't miss.  except it does.  the script makes no sense, the songs are poor, and the characters are 1-dimensional.  not the best effort of this genre.

text: a friendly alien comes to earth to scout it out (or something), but gets stranded due to a mishap.  then govt agents come hunting for him, so he needs help to escape and return to his home planet.  sound familiar?  ET?  well, this film shares its basic plot with ET.  while ET was basically a kid's movie, the scattered running around for no reason did not bother anyone.  but this one pretends it is for adults.  but the plot has holes you could fly a space cruiser through.  you keep asking yourself: why is he/she doing that? why would they want to dissect someone who has morphed into an earthling?  then there are the magic glowing marbles that can do . . . who knows.  the two leads are appealing enough but the plot is pretty annoying.
description: ["Upon crash-landing on Earth, an alien space traveler takes on the appearance of a young widow's husband, and enlists her help to get across the country and avoid the authorities. As the government tracks them down, the unlikely pair begin to bond."]

text: a nice blend of european and american cultures.  a spanish immigrant to paris, a nouveau riche american couple who lord it over everyone else, some french people who have french scruples about love and marriage.  throw in a kind of cinderella story of a poor woman who attracts a prince of sorts, and has an evil and jealous stepmother.  of course things don't go quite the way they do in fairy tales.  at first i was disappointed by the ending but after a little thought realized it was kind of a good one, or at least realistic.  not only entertaining, but also has some things to think about.
description: ['Anne and Bob, a well-to-do American couple, have just moved to a beautiful manor house in romantic Paris. To impress their sophisticated friends, they decide to host a lavish dinner party, but must disguise their maid as a noblewoman to even out the number of guests. title_y: The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet
description: ["A ten-year-old cartographer secretly leaves his family's ranch and travels across the country aboard a freight train to receive a prestigious award at the Smithsonian Institute."]

text: a sweet and poignant, and sometimes grating, look inside a hospice.  gives the viewer insights as to life there.  comes off as more of a play, and that is meant as a compliment.  saddest of all is watching the slow death of a young man, with his wife right by his side every minute, and the love they share is palpable, even as they know he is dying.  my only complaint is with the grating voice of cassell, which took me out of the mood.
description: ["Dying is hell - and Alvin's going to make sure everyone knows it. Academy Award nominees Seymour Cassell & Alfre Woodard star. AARP Movies for Grownups Award-winner."]

text: quite a nice little story.  still amazing that women were ever denied the right to vote anywhere at anytime, much less a civilized country late in the 20th century.  interesting to watch the awakening in all of the women as they deal with this problem and turn things around.  film goes into the individual families as well, showing how the issue might have affected relationships.  makes you think as well as feel.
description: ['An uplifting, empowering and crowd-pleasing drama set in Switzerland in the early 1970s, about a seemingly unremarkable housewife from a quaint village who must learn to become an unflinching suffragette leader. Winner of the Audience Award for Best Feature at the 2017 Tribeca International Film Festival.']

text: quite a nice little film.  the characters, although a little bizarre, are believable, as is their behavior.  love that they used non-hollywood types for actors, makes the whole thing more credible.  the ending is realistic, as is the way people behave here.  draws you in, wanting the best for everyone.
description: ['Chet is a 28 year old agoraphobic man and still lives with his mother. When Mom moves away Chet has to get a roommate. Enter Maggie. A volatile female Marine with her own personal issues. The two become emotionally entangled as they struggle to escape from their self-made prisons.']

text: as advertised, a spoof of those old mutated monster movies, with stereotypical characters and situations, that are amusing because they are only one step further than the movies themselves.  the monster, in particular, was a classic, the outfit, the costume, the way he moved, etc etc.  amusing and laugh out loud at times.

text: this was a lot of fun.  terrific sendup of those old 1950s grade B space/monster movies.  they seemed to particularly goof on the Blob in a number of ways.  the cars, the signs, the clothes, the behavior - all pitch-perfect.  especially loved the monster, or "space ghost" as one of the characters referred to it.  has it all: the hip teenagers, the skeptical sheriff, the redneck citizens, the bratty kid, the eerie monster music.  and you just know the film-makers had a hoot doing this.
description: ['After crash landing on the outskirts of a desert town, an alien enlists the help of a waitress to recapture a monster that has escaped the wreck.']

Other than that, I won't say much about the plot or reveal any spoilers. The movie could be 20-30 minutes shorter and it would have been just as good, maybe even better. It takes a long time to get to the good stuff. And there is a scene where at least a dozen security guards are defeated in one way or another. Three or four would have been plenty. text:
Even if it takes 20 years, revenge is sweet. That is the message of this movie. And one of its lessons is don't mess with writers because they will write you into their novel and they will mess you up right back, worse than you could ever have dreamed of.

Other reviewers have given descriptions of this movie. I won't bother with that. I will, however, point out some things that are ****WARNING: SPOILERS**** maybe not immediately apparent. The viewer learns approximately two-thirds of the way through the film that the daughter mentioned in the novel actually exists and is alive. What we don't learn until almost the end of the movie is that when when Susan (Amy Adams) left Tony (Jake Gyllenhaal for Hutton (Armie Hammer), she was pregnant with Tony's child. One wonders if it was a condition of the relationship between Susan and Hutton that she abort the child, or if Susan did not want to have a continuing tie to Tony. They already had one child, so there would always be a connection. However, it is clear that both by writing this novel and by standing Susan up at the end, Tony has achieved his revenge.

I was brought up in an evangelical Christian household and therefore I was fed a lot of ideas about forgiveness, turning the other cheek, etc., etc. For many years, even though I left the church at age fourteen, I still believed in the basic goodness of humans and I believed that being kind to one's fellow human beings was...well, was the human thing to do. I still give people I meet the benefit of the doubt until they show me that they are not a good person. At that point, I generally walk away and simply do not associate with them any more. If, however, they do something to hurt me or someone I love, I have no problem with seeking revenge, in whatever form seems appropriate. Years ago if I had seen this movie, I would have felt that the character in Tony's novel was wrong to seek revenge. No more. Some beings that walk on two legs are not human and should be put down like the demons they are.

This story reminded me of the fable of the scorpion and the frog. For those who are not familiar with it, it goes like this: A scorpion asks a frog if the frog will let him ride across a pond on the frog's back. The frog says, "No, you're a scorpion, you'll sting me." Scorpion says, "Don't be ridiculous, if I sting you, we'll both die." Frog is suspicious and wary but finally agrees. text:
Interesting. Barbara Gordon's memoir turned motion picture has added memorably to the collective body of evidence that benzodiazepines inflict grave harm if taken long term and even worse so in higher dosages, despite being doctor directed or sanctioned. Many aspects of the film seem dated (especially the jarring horror movie sound effects) but the lived experience of problematic benzo withdrawal sadly remains as relevant-- if not more so-- than 3.5 decades ago.

I felt dismayed that the highest drama of her acute cold turkey withdrawal from daily 60 mg. Valium (diazepam) dosage built up over 10 years of physical dependency was entirely overshadowed by the domestic violence of her abusive alcoholic live in boyfriend's control maneuvers. It greatly detracted from the supposed main subject of the film. However, it's based on her true story and often times in life issues compile and collide together in disastrous ways.

Ideally, medicine would be practiced as a collaborative effort between medical practitioner and client with full disclosure (informed consent) to the benefit-risk ratio of various treatments or protocols. What most frequently happens is--as depicted in this film-- where patients get blindly led down a path of the allopathic 'there's a pill for every ill' motto with no advertised exit ramp that can then be extremely difficult to extricate oneself from after years of habit. Gordon realized one day that after a decade of compliance to a proscribed direction that actually she's functionally worse off than before she began and wants out. Only she had no clue as to what lay in wait for her in getting off her prescription medication.

text: Stunningly cinematic from beginning to end.  Having read Philip Roth books before and having seen the movie "The Ice Storm" previously, I had a better background knowledge of what to expect creatively than I think of some of the other reviewers who may have not recognized all the complexity and innuendo surrounding the film.  Much like "Dr. Zhivago", the love story plot highlights and masterfully reveals many layers of social commentary.  The two main characters are beholden to submit to forces and structures much more established and powerful than they are, and thus, both end up betrayed by those decisions made on their behalf in accordance to the prevailing order of the day.  Like all good art, the ideas conveyed about human nature, good and evil, and the extent of free will within a context extend far beyond the time and place depicted in the setting.  The acting and direction left nothing more to be desired... fantastic!

text:
Considering the hodgepodge writing that steals ideas from anywhere and everywhere, and the less than stellar acting - not all the time, but frankly, a lot of the time - I’m amazed so many famous people guested on this show; I can only assume because it was popular. In that way, I compare it to McDonald’s. Just because it’s popular doesn’t mean it’s good.

This show starts off with promise, as we get to see Allison coming to terms with her psychic abilities and starting to use them to solve crimes. But somewhere along the line, (season two?) the writers begin stealing ideas from movies (Oh no wait! Paying homage!) including a cringe-worthy and poorly done rip-off of The Notebook) and the story lines just get more and more unbelievable: switching bodies, possession, time travel, medical maladies related to murderers, etc.. Yet even when there is an attempt at lightheartedness or the storyline is bordering on the ridiculous (often), there is always a high level of drama, graphic violence, and darkness which hangs over this show like a cloud.

Part of this darkness stems from the character of Allison Dubois herself, who is completely self-centered and self-absorbed around her dreaming and crime fighting, continually waking Joe in the middle of the night to dissect her latest dream. Together, she and Joe exhibit a complete lack of parenting: The oldest daughter spends at least the first two seasons verbally abusing her younger sister - constantly calling Brigette stupid, etc. And the parents never tell her to stop. The kids together are constantly screaming and fighting and not once do the parents ever tell them to be quiet or to stop fighting; they are too absorbed in their own problems to pay attention and parent.

Later there are the obligatory stories of each child dealing with their burgeoning psychic powers (Yawn).

The one bright spot in this show is Jake Weber who plays Joe Dubois. He is extremely likable, his character has the patience of a saint, and he’s the only actor in the nuclear Dubois “family” who is always believable. (By contrast, if I have to watch Patricia Arquette fake cry one more time…ugh.) I only wish the writers wouldn’t make him so dumb. (He’s completely bewildered the millionth time Allison wakes with some strange malady?)

Overall, Medium is watchable, but it’s a lot like junk food: It’s seems fun at first but in the end leaves you feeling slightly sick and like you need a cleanse.

text: Bravo to this excellent series! This show has at least 6 episodes, and I was fooled into thinking that I could watch all 6 when I signed up for Masterpiece on Amazon today.  Wrong!  I loved watching Miss Scarlet on the PBS app, but wanted to see new episodes so I went on Amazon thinking that I could get them all (it doesn't state otherwise).  I found out that as of January 25th, only two episodes are available.  I must wait until next Sunday to see episode 3 and on it goes every week until they are all released.  Perhaps if more people complain Amazon will make this more clear.  In the meantime, I just want you to know that this series is highly entertaining and well done!  I love following Miss Scarlet as she tries to solve police cases before the police are able to do so--sort of like Sherlock Holmes in female form with the same time setting in England.  She is smart, darling, and bold, which are three things a woman ought not to be in 19th century England while the laws of coverture (English common law regarding women's rights) were still in effect, and the culture was male-dominated.  I highly recommend this series!

text: As writer Neil Gaiman famously said, “Make it dark, make it grim, make it tough, but then, for the love of God, tell a joke.”  I don't know if he said it before or after Young Dracula was made, but this thoroughly enjoyable show was clearly put together with that mindset.  Young Dracula is about growing up, parents, siblings, school, crushes, friends, loves, making choices and making mistakes.  The first two seasons are lighter and based on the problems and issues someone the young age (about 10?) of the protagonist (a family-misfit who just wants to be normal) might face, with a twist because of the whole vampirism thing.  Later seasons find high-school-age Vlad (young Dracula) facing tougher issues and decisions as he faces impending adulthood. The humor comes mostly via Count Dracula and the family servant, Renfield; the latter is almost entirely gross-humor comic relief but the actor who plays the single-father Count Dracula is able to slip effortlessly in presence and tone from a kind of effete aristocrat (wherein is most of the humor) into someone with voice and expression of a stone-cold killer (as befits a 600 year old vampire.)  Humor aside, I'd be surprised if you didn't cry at times, I certainly did.  And although the show is marketed as being for children, I'm a grandmother and I absolutely enjoyed every minute of the series.  (NOTE: I will warn you that there are two episodes out of order in the 5th season -- but you'll figure that out. text:
I watched this documentary for the first time a couple of weeks ago,and wascompletely charmed by Ridgway's sisters-in-law, Doreen and Tina, and their daughters, Ridgway's nieces, Kristen and Jennifer.

I was born, and still live in Seattle.

Anyone from Seattle knows the local (unfair) stereotype of the population south of Seattle city limits. The farther south you go, you encounter mullets, bad grammer, etc

These women are anything BUT that, and certainly not anybody you would expect to be related to Gary Ridgway.

They all seemed very intelligent, sophisticated, and appear to be sincere, nice women.

In the 1980s, during the height of Ridgway's reign of terror, the area where he grew up, still lived, and found most of his victims, was experiencing growth, but had a history of small family farms, and still had a lot of rural areas like the Green River, and maintained a small town feel with a pretty tight knit community.

Ridgway's parent's, as well as his siblings, 2 brothers and their families, also still lived in the area.
I think this documentary was part of a very worthwile and sincere project. The women wanted to try to do what they could as family, while Gary was alive, to try to get information he might not have been willing to give authorities, especially after being in prison for about 13 or 14 years.
They hoped through arranged telephone conversations from prison, they could get Gary to give ANY information, and ideally, reveal locations of the bodies of women still missing for more than 30 years.

Kristen, and Doreen resemble each other quite a bit, and it is clear throughout the film, they are mother and daughter.

However, I think the director did a pretty good job at distracting from the fact that the other 2 women, Tina and Jennifer, are also mother and daughter. I think Ive figured out the reason.

Jennifer (probably married) used the last name Cox, not Ridgway like her mother,Tina,

Jennifer and Tina, her mom, virtually do not talk to each other, and do not acknowledge each other throughout the film. They are not introduced as mother and daughter.
Tina's husband, and Jennifer's dad, the youngest Ridgway brother, was REFERRED to many times, but his NAME was not mentioned ONCE by anybody.
It is perfectly understandable that he would want to maintain his privacy, however, I think it was done for the same reason Jennifer and Tina were not connected.

After watching this film again, and some other accounts of the case, I started putting together some disturbing details.

In 1982, five women's bodies were found in the Green River almost simultaneously.

Dave Reichert was the detective from the King County Sheriff, sent to the scene when the first woman was spotted in the river by two boys riding their bikes.

Soon, another person stumbled upon 2 more. A fourth was spotted by another witness, and while at the crime scene, Reichert was walking through some brush and actually tripped over the 5th body. Five womens bodies had been discovered in one month from July to August of 1982. Four of them were found within 2 days.

The King County Sheriffs who had jurisdiction, immediately knew they had a serial killer, and were not equipped to handle a case of that magnitude, as bodies started being discovered regularly.

Tomas Guillen, who co-wrote, "The Search for the Green River Killer", said the police barely had time to investigate, identify victims, and follow-up on thousands of leads, because they were constantly excavating crime scenes.

By the end of 1983, 11 bodies had been discovered, and during 1984, varying accounts of between 22 and 49 bodies had been found. In 2005, Ridgway plead guilty to 48 of the murders, and is in prison iin Walla Walla, Washington. Currently, Ridgway is believed to be responsible for the deaths of 90 women.

In 1983, a pervasive fear throughout Western Washington was building as body after body was being discovered.

At one point in the film, Tina is alone, talking about walking home from work around 11PM in 1983, near the area where women were disappearing and their bodies turning up.

A guy pulls up in his truck and offers her a ride. She declines.
Tina, again, by herself during this recollection, says he persisted becoming visibly angry when she continued to decline. He finally leaves, and she walks to a phone booth just yards away and calls her parents to come pick her up.

Later in film, she is on that street, showing Kristen and Jennifer the site.
(Talking with Kristen)

She points to the phone booth she used, still there, and says one of Ridgway's victims disappeared from that SAME phone booth ONE HALF HOUR
after she called her parents that night.

Tina did NOT know Gary.
Tina had NOT met, and did NOT know Gary's brother, her future husband, at that time.

Again, Tina being interviewed alone, recounts when she started dating her future husband, Gary's brother, and was introduced to Gary.

Tina recognized Gary, and after a bit, placed him as the guy in the truck.

She went on to say that Gary was "a little strange" but she didn't think too much about it.
They do not say AT ALL when she met and started dating Gary's brother, but it had to be not too long after her encounter with Ridgway in his truck.

This is what I missed the first time, and was confused by:

Later, Jennifer is interviewed ALONE, and SHE talks about her mother being introduced to Gary Ridgway for the first time.

As I said, Jennifer and Tina have NOT interacted AT ALL. Jennifer does NOT refer to Tina as her mother, OR the story her mother told about being introduced to Ridgway for the first as his brothers date after her encounter with him in his truck
So Jennifer talks about how her dad was living with Doreen and Gregg, Gary's older brother.
They hosted a Halloween party that her mother (Tina) attends as Gary's BROTHER'S DATE.
She encounters a man in a long hooded cape and a green mask. He is introduced as her date's brother, Gary.

The cape and hood had leaves, and twigs taped all over it. Jennifer recounts that her mother asks him who he is supposed to be. He answers, "I'm "The Riverman", a name Ted Bundy coined for "The Green River Killer"

After watching the first time, even though there were only three brothers, I was confused about Jennifer's parentage.

Now, Tina, recounting first being introduced to Gary as her date and future husbands brother, WITHOUT mentioning the little detail that it was at a Halloween party where Ridgway was dressed as the Green River Killer, had basically tried to abduct her, and just saying he was "kind of strange but didn't think much more about it" sounds like a lie, sadly.

By Tina and Jennifer not interacting at all, NOT being clearly identified as mother and daughter, Gary's younger brother, Jennifer's dad and Tina's husband, never being referred to by name, by Tina especially, was all done on purpose, to make Tina and Jennifer's accounts sound like two different stories about 2 different people.
Doreen, Kristen's mom DID briefly admit that there were signs that Gary could be the killer, but she was in denial
However, the main theme, and by all accounts of the family, including Tina and Jennifer, Ridgway was the poster boy for the nice family man.
In the beginning of the film, Kristen talks about how Ridgway not only ripped apart the victims' families, but their own family as well. She goes on to say the the four women hadn't been together in ten years, after being, by their accounts, a very close, happy family.
Kristen said when Gary was arrested in 2002, she was in a terrible state, hiding out, ashamed of her name, ashamed to share his DNA.

The whole Ridgway family had lived in that small community for well over 50 years. It must have been devastating on so many levels.
I don't think it would be possible for Tina, especially, to participate in the film and not talk about her encounter with Ridgway. The story about her first introduction to him in his Halloween costume being told by Tina would leave glaring questions, but is too good to leave out, so they try to distract that the Halloween story is about her.
I cannot imagine continuing to date a guy whose brother had tried to abduct me, during a time a serial killer, the most prolific in US history, is operating in my neighborhood, or not reporting him to the police.
Why has the Ridgway family been, "ripped apart", as Kristen said. They had a history of being very close. Adversity CAN bring people closer. Why did it not in this already close family?
Gary was an early suspect in the GRK, but they lacked hard evidence, and after being arrested twice for solicitation, in 1987, he agreed to take a lie detector test...... and passed. SO did Ted Bundy. Ridgway was shelved.
What I wonder is who knew about Tina's encounter with Gary? Did Tina keep it to herself? Did she tell his brother? Maybe there was a family decision to keep it quiet. Maybe SOME knew. Maybe others didn't find out until it was too late, and have to live with a responsibility for lost lives.........I think there is another story about the Ridgway family that could prove quite intetesting.

text:
I think the Farrelly Brothers are somewhat misunderstood.

I actually saw "Hall Pass" a couple of years ago. It was either free on HBO or I rented it. I don't remember.

What I DO remember, is that it was a rather bland movie, until the scene at the gym, when Owen Wilson was in the men's locker room, sitting in the spa, which was at floor level.

He got stuck on the intake valve, and started to panic. I think he called out for help................................

Two guys that were in a "state of complete undress" rescued him.

Because the spa was floor level, the scene was shot so all the audience saw of the rescuers, was from a few inches above the waist, downward............................

I've seen several Farrelly Brothers movies. My birthday is at a difficult time of year for a party, so what I started doing, was requiring friends and family to attend a matinee, of the most ridiculous comedy in theaters at the time, and afterward, we all go to lunch.

We've seen "Dumb and Dumber", "Ace Ventura", etc. You get the picture.

One year, there were ten of us............, including my best friend of 45 years, my 89 year old mother, sister, erudite brother-in-law, etc.

There is genius in this practice. Since I never get an actual party, I at least get the pleasure of subjecting my loved ones to sophomoric, gross-out humor for 2 hours! I overheard my above mentioned "best friend", tell another guest, while we were all leaving the theater after "Ace........" "I actually gagged..................."

I also got to see my BIL, who likes to think of himself as someone who wouldn't be caught dead at a movie in this "genre", not able to keep himself from laughing at gags in "Dumb and Dumber". I was in HEAVEN!

But the really great part, is that if I don't get an actual party, it is at least an activity, and nobody has to feel uncomfortable if they didn't like it. THESE movies, the group is blasting before they leave their seats!

At "Dumb and Dumber", my mom was sitting about 4 guests away from me in my row.

During the infamous, protracted, diarrhea scene, I bent over to see her reaction, and she had her head down, with her fingers in her ears.

After the movie, I asked her if she was okay. She said, "Oh, yes." "I was just afraid I was going to have an accident." She actually thought some of it was very funny.

But I digress. "Hall Pass" just seemed like a "white bread" comedy, until the gym scene, and the view of the two rescuers, included "full frontal nudity" and a very good look at two VERY large, semi-erect penises.

In an INSTANT, I knew it HAD to be a Farrelly Brother's movie! I wouldn't put it past those two, to purposely write a boring comedy, possibly leave their names off the opening credits........., just so they could lull the audience into a catatonic state, then WHAM, wake 'em up with two of the biggest units I've ever seen, and KNOW that loyal fans would recognize their "signature" anywhere! NOBODY else could EVER beat them in utterly tasteless humor!

title_x: The Computer Science / Math is 95% wrong
text:
I wanted to like this movie. I'm a computer scientist who works on NP complete problems in my research. The premise of the film attracted me to watch it. However, the writers should have sought experts as consultants. They clearly did not as they got the theory of NP completeness almost entirely wrong.

The major flaw is that the 4 mathematicians who are portrayed as having solved the question of whether or not P=NP, rely on what they describe as a nondeterministic machine in their supposed proof that P is equal to NP. Although the N in NP means nondeterministic, the theory of NP completeness assumes a Turing Machine, which is deterministic. Although they don't use the term quantum computer in the movie, what they describe as their nondeterministic machine must be a quantum computer. Quantum computers are not Turing Machines. Solving an NP complete problem in polynomial time on a quantum computer does NOT prove P is equal to NP.

They did get something right though. If P is ever proved equal to NP, then the ramifications of that on cryptography, science, etc are as explained by the 4 mathematician characters. It would have both profoundly positive impacts as well as profoundly negative impacts.

It is a shame that the writers focused too much on their misunderstanding of NP completeness theory. If they instead explicitly described the machine as a quantum computer and dropped all of the solving P vs NP nonsense, the story would go in the same direction and lead to the same set of potential consequences of the mathematicians' work. Quantum computers, at least theoretically, can be used to solve NP complete, and thus all NP problems, efficiently. That is true even if P doesn't equal NP. This leads to the same debate over the potential great benefits to humanity and potentially severe prospects of misuse that was the focus of the characters in the movie.

text:
I meant to get around to watching this for a while but I didn't finally do it until Boxing Day. I had enough confidence that I bought it sight unseen. I was (mostly) not disappointed. It takes more cues from the Nolan movies than the Burton ones as it's a grittier, more realistic Gotham. The story is like if you took Year One, Hush, and a few other comics stories and put them in a blender. Like the Tom Holland Spider-Man, they dispensed with the origin, probably figuring we've seen that enough already. So this is in Year Two, where Batman and Lt. Gordon are trying to fight crime. But then a new villain called the Riddler starts killing prominent people and leaving clues to a deep, dark secret, one that might even implicate the Waynes. In trying to track down the Riddler, Batman meets Selina Kyle, aka Catwoman--though again we never use that name--and they team up, which includes some kissing.

While I liked it, I have a few criticisms. First, I don't know what Batman's armor is made of, but there's no way anything in current existence could get shot the number of times it does and survive. Second, the final act is kind of a letdown as it involves a manmade natural disaster and Batman facing a bunch of randos, which kind of diminishes the stakes; this also drags a bit. Third, there's not a ton of development to Alfred or Gordon. Still, it's not enough to really bring it down too much. (3.5/5) (Fun Facts: Like the Nolan movies, this was partially shot in Chicago and heavily hints we'll see the Joker in the sequel. Near the end Batman injects himself with something green to give him a boost; was this Venom and does this hint we could see Bane in a future movie? And if we see Bane, might we get Azrael too? Unlikely, but I can dream...)

text: I came upon this film rather casually - it showed up in my "recommendations," yet had never heard of it before. It possessed everything I expect from a lush and romantic British period piece, and much more.  What I hadn't anticipated is where this WW1 film would take me: A journey through the raw and rare true-life witness of a woman who lived through it all, and lost so much - her lover, her brother, her male friends.  All to the most devastating war in history. She abandons her very unique and privileged acceptance as a literary woman, and would-be writer at Oxford University, to volunteer as a nurse, first at home in Britain treating the hopeful wounded, with a chance at real survival, to the front where the conditions were horrific and the severely wounded were hopelessly savaged by battle injuries with too little medical/surgical help to save them, let alone make their death's peaceful.  Without saying more - lest I spoil the movie - do not expect a quick happy ending to this engrossing drama. But will share that with this experience came the gift of the remarkable woman and writer who has gifted us with the autobiographical novel from which this based, "Testament of Youth," by  Vera Brittain.

title_x: Doesn't do Mr. Paulides cause justice
text: As an avid listeners to David Paulides interviews and viewers of his Youtube channel, my friend and I were excited to finally watch this together.  Paulides is a thorough and thoughtful investigator with strong credibility and a deep compassion for the victims.  He's also a great speaker and presents evidence very well, particularly the patterns and similarities between cases that make up the evidence that is Missing 411.  He's wonderful at connecting the dots for the listener/reader but careful to walk the line of allowing you to come up with your own theory.  He's long been guarded of what his theory behind the vast collection of abnormal National Parks Missing Person Cases is.  None of that was present in this film.  I know he teamed up with his son to make this film and I have to say it was beautiful shot.  The footage/camera work is gorgeous, as is the lighting and sound quality.  The problem is that nothing is presented.  For some reason the cases explored are all male children, which makes no sense given Mr. Paulides normally presents cases of both genders of all ages.  They don't talk about the patterns or even present that material.  Nothing about water, boulder fields, being the last person in a row of hikers, etc.  It's really strange that they left that out.  It feels more like a Dateline episode as it focuses primarily on one case which the details of are told again and again and again, while intercutting other stories. All the cases they presented are easily dismissed as being the fault of negligent adults who weren't watching the small children properly.  One even includes a mentally challenged pedophile former convict, so you can't help but assume he did something awful.  That particular child also has a creepy Great-Grandfather who refers to the missing 2 year old consistently as "the kid" and laughs frequently while answering questions about his disappearance.  Further, the Great-Grandfather refuses to be on camera.  WTF?  It's also strange that they focused on cases where the families were all of rural-lower-socio-economic circumstances.  You'd think they would have used more of a cross-section.  Basically it feels like they could only get these few families to agree to be interviewed and so they made the movie with the footage they had instead of taking the time to get more interviews so it was a stronger thesis.  I hope they will make another movie and will fix these issues.  I feel terrible for all of the parents/families who have lost someone and Mr. Paulides work is so important.  He's a wonderful person with a strong-skillset and the ability to draw attention to his cause.  I just don't think this movie is doing that.  I really hope they will get more interviews about missing adults and recut this film with that new footage and make a sequel that includes all of the patterns of these cases, as well as all of his tips for how to avoid going missing.  Also, it was very hard to follow who was who and which case they belonged to.  It would have been nice to have names appear on screen each time a talking head reappeared.  Many of the rural people look very similar so it was hard to remember who was who.
description: ['Based on the books series written by David Paulides Missing 411 chronicles the unsolved yet eerily similar disappearances of five children in the wilds of North America across multiple decades.']

text:
I didn't know what to expect when I watched this. I remember when it was still fresh and was being hyped as so great, but never saw it. And given the pace I may not have liked it when I was younger, anyway.

Bassett only made a brief appearance despite the thumbnail drawing people to click on it to watch. I found that peculiar but then thought about the fact this was probably made before she starred in her hit movies.

It's not a thrill or exciting and there's no real big build up (and subsequent overflow) of anything. Most movies and well, stories for that matter, have climaxes near the end. This one has....struggles and revelations. Those are dealt with as they occur.

I'm gonna tell you what I liked most about this movie. It wasn't the usual troupe of the unfortunate, underprivileged black woman that is cursed to work for the spoiled, cruel southern white woman and she has to set her straight about "the real world".

The story works out that this could have easily been so but the movie actually dealt with the way real life is here in the modern world. They were two women from different worlds, who didn't even necessarily fit into their own worlds, but weren't bitter about it either. Both of them equally had to be real with each other or it wasn't going to work. They both needed each other and deep down they knew it. That's why they made it work. Because of that, it did work and they got along like actual human beings get along in the real world.

Don't get me wrong, they did point out the two local southern women that came to visit her and boy were they on point! They were so on point about everything we hate about the South I had to laugh (I can say that as I'm a Southerner). You could cut the overly proper, controlling passive-aggressiveness with a knife! This is the kicker of why I liked that; it showed these two women as only a PART of the South, not the South. There is so much more to us than what Hollywood would love you to think sometimes. This movie displayed that.

The lady in this film had been around, and she accepted nothing less than straight forwardness, and yet at the same time was not going to be bossed around. She was used to being independent and yet as a movie star she had some "spoiled" issues that she had to face. The "black servant" role (or whatever you'd like to call it - she wasn't a "servant" in this movie) had to show her this and teach her about this certain type of hardship, but it wasn't because of race. It was because of her own life experiences (which gets revealed later of course). It wasn't a black to white kind of thing, it was a human to human thing.

I'm baffled as to how Hollywood could have made such a REAL movie and stayed oh so slightly away from the temptation to make race, sex, sexual orientation, religion, etc an issue (and all of this was there to play with as they usually do).

This a very mature movie for mature people with a head on their shoulders and an attention span of more than a couple of minutes. If you are over all the social issues Hollywood still thinks to this day you need to be preached to about, and want to cut through the crap and appreciate a movie about relationships between human beings, this will be one of your go to's.

As others have pointed out, I thought the ending was kind of abrupt. But maybe that's in keeping with the them of the movie. What else was there supposed to be? Running off into the sunset with flowers in their hair?

title_x: I REALLY enjoyed this Christmas movie.
text:
The grandfather figure (Chap) is dealing with the recent loss of his wife and it has made him reclusive and grouchy. Circumstances force him to put aside his hurt in favor of helping others and processing his grief in a healthier way. I really enjoyed Steve J. Young as Chap. He seemed like someone you would just want to hug in church. Cassidy, the little girl, knows NOTHING, absolutely nothing of the true Christmas story and she begins to learn all about it in such a sweet way that it was a genuine pleasure to watch. The villain, Eddie, does a good job of being believable. I only wish they had called the sheriff on him at some point. I cannot say I am a fan of actress Tara Reid who played the long-distance daughter, Laura, sporting raccoon-looking eye-makeup, but she was not the main focus thankfully because in my opinion, her acting was sub-par compared with the rest of the cast. Overall, I needed a tissue a couple of times, I appreciated the rural Kentucky ranch town that I would welcome visiting, loved how the “family” came together, the kindness of nice-guy Tyler (played by Randy Wayne) whose role is appropriate… showing a bit of romantic interest without being over the top because it is such a new relationship and I liked that. The manger story was thoughtfully and gently shared in a unique way. Although it is not a big box office budget it does not come off as a cheesy low-budget film. Most of the actors did a good job. I would watch it again and recommend it to friends and family.
🎄 {For parents with young children, there is one scene where Chap gets punched in the face and is knocked unconscious, head bleeding from whatever he fell on. This happens when Eddie shows up in the dark at the manger, so you can have your kids look away at that point}.

text:
This is the sort of movie we expect from Matt Damon - hard-hitting, fast paced, intense. The supporting cast was not as good as Damon, but many are not as talented as he. Can't hold that against them. Kinnear did an okay job. Some of the others, according to a blurb at the beginning, were actual military men who had served in Iraq and/or Afghanistan.
A number of reviewers took umbridge at the depiction of the political back and forth between competing points of view. With no desire to cause trouble, I do think a few points bear examination. It is common knowledge now that there were no weapons of mass destruction, and that the accusations were lies to convince the American public of the need to invade Iraq. The first "governor" of Iraq was a career politician with, apparently, little or no experience with war. I don't know if he alone decided to disband the Iraqi military (probably not), but he announced it. Many did not want to impose another Bathist led military, but many others thought it unwise not to use the Iraqi Army to help regain order and control of the country. I have heard that the rejected military men formed the core of ISIS. I don't know it that's true but it makes sense, and they did show up on the scene with a considerable arsenal of weapons.
Anyway, if you like Damon action movies, you'll probably enjoy this one.

text:
This is an agenda driven documentary, so if you are in their camp, you will probably like the film and agree with the conclusions. I agree with some points; I do not support trophy hunting of any species. And let it be said that the most successful conservationists, the ones who were the first to recognize the issues and get them remedied, have always been the hunters, not the couch potatoes. Theodore Roosevelt comes quickly to mind – an ardent hunter and an ardent conservationist.
Now to questions raised. First, do bears see human beings as prey animals? Not normally, but an old bear that cannot hunt strong or fast prey might see a human as a potential meal. I think that is what happened to Timothy Treadwell and his girlfriend, but I did not follow that closely. Another exception may be made for the polar bear. To a polar bear, any other creature is a potential meal. Second, have there been unprovoked attacks on humans? Yes. On two consecutive nights in 1967 in Glacier National Park, two sleeping young women, miles apart, were dragged from their tents, mauled, and partially eaten by grizzly bears, and a young man was injured but not killed. Further, look up the account of the friend of a man who raised and trained a grizzly bear. The friend was assured that he could stand close to the bear who was not a danger. Suddenly, for no obvious reason, the bear attacked the friend who subsequently died from the attack. I saw a video of the attack and it was chilling. The message that bears are cute and cuddly and not potentially dangerous is itself quite dangerous to stupid urbanite viewers who might think they, too, could cavort with bears.
There are a surprising number of experts in this film who present questionable views. I’ll limit myself here - one man stated, as if a given fact, that the bears that attacked the Lewis and Clark expedition were the bears that had been wounded by the men. He does not state his source – and how could there be a source except the bears themselves - so it must be something he concluded on his own and passes on as a fact. He also said that the rifle shot hardly penetrated the bears. Again, where he got that is anyone’s guess, for it is a foolish misconception. So, by his reasoning, the shot just made them mad, and the bears bided their time and came back for revenge. As anthropomorphic as that it, it is interesting, but foolish, reasoning. First, the shot would have penetrated the bear. Second, in the heat of the moment, an injured bear would attack a person if the person were within striking distance, but most injured animals, bear, deer, etc., go off and die; they seldom survive a gunshot wound.
What is the bottom line? The film’s argument is that bear hunting should be banned. Personally, I don’t agree. I do agree that trophy hunting should be ended, but not sustenance hunting.
description: ['First Nations, environmentalists, scientists and ecotourism operators are fighting a battle to ban grizzly bear hunting in British Columbia. Standing in their way is a population obsessed with blood sports, the lucrative hunting tourism industry, and the myth of the bear as a vicious and dangerous animal. Naturalist Charlie Russell leads the campaign to rebrand the bear in an effort to save it.']

It is said to be commercial whaling, but what were/are the commercial benefits. All they spoke of was whale meat as food, and it isn’t a very popular food item in most of the world. Where is the benefit?
As for content, most hunters genuinely care about the health and overall wellbeing of the target population. I did not hear even a hint of that from the whalers. Did I miss something? All I heard was, ‘I will hunt whales because I can’ and, ‘I don’t even care if I lose money (on expensive trips to Japan), I will hunt whales because I can’. I support a hunter’s right to hunt (non-endangered species), but what I just saw wasn’t about hunting as a sport. It was about hunting as some sort of national identity thing. Not a good enough argument, IMO.

text: Interesting and informative. Would that it were simple to change people’s ways of thinking. When I was a child, woodlands were viewed as sources of financial wealth. (This continues to today.) Unless one were going to farm a tract, one did not buy land that was treeless because that wealth had already been extracted. But I should add that clearcutting was not as common back then, and so the value of the forest cover to the surrounding environment was maintained to a degree. No one I knew would have considered the forest to have any other sort of wealth, except perhaps some aesthetic value, but certainly not the metaphysical, philosophical wealth as touched on in this documentary. I’m not speaking against such wealth; I found that portion of the documentary particularly interesting. It made me wish I knew more about the Druids and their religion. I have always wondered why the Romans were so intent on wiping the Druids out completely. I’m sorry for rambling. I do recommend you watch this documentary and that you show it to your children. Not enough of us take climate change seriously.
